1	ai-writer 0.7.5 — Codex 文件创作工具（Node.js >=20，无额外依赖）
2	
3	init --path 新目录 --kind novel|screenplay|history|essay --title 作品名 [--mode long|standard]
4	  建立作品和随附工具，不覆盖已有目录。明确长篇/跨卷时用long，提前组织全书骨架、卷契约和近期细纲。
5	plan --project 作品目录 --input 细纲.json
6	  保存下一章、场或篇的细纲。
7	context --project 作品目录 [--purpose discussion|draft|revision] [--unit 1] [--max-chars 40000] [--out .writer/drafts/context-1.json]
8	  discussion恢复任务/范围/决策；draft及revision须有授权和细纲。超预算不截断。out可选，写新的内部JSON可读入口，不覆盖旧输入。
9	record-template --project 作品目录 --unit 1 --draft 正文/0001-来信.md [--out .writer/drafts/record-1.json]
10	  动笔前取得登记模板。路径/哈希自动填，未变事实保留；按实际正文填摘要与changes，不誊写全快照。
11	record-preview --project 作品目录 --input 登记.json [--out .writer/drafts/preview-1.json]
12	  只读预检，复用record校验并展示实际事实差异、未变项和待补字段；不自动刷新过期哈希，不证明语义无变化。
13	long-enable-preview --project 作品目录
14	  只读预览长篇迁移与估计journal体积，不创建备份、不改状态；取消即停止，实际启用仍需授权及当前revision。
15	record --project 作品目录 --input 登记.json
16	  填写写前模板中的实际摘要与追踪，然后顺序登记正文。不要从手册抄写假哈希。
17	status --project 作品目录 [--view compact|full]
18	  查看进度、过期来源、未登记正文和建议下一步。
19	check --project 作品目录
20	  检查机械一致性与未登记正文；不裁定文学质量。
21	rewind --project 作品目录 --from 1 --expected-revision 当前修订号
22	  备份并作废指定单元及后续追踪，保留正文。schema4及以上须先建立独立修订区，在该区带revision-token回退；不在主稿直接执行。旧协议兼容原路径。
23	export --project 作品目录 --out 作品目录外的新目录
24	  导出已登记草稿，列出未纳入的正文；不覆盖旧导出。
25	long-enable --project 作品目录 --expected-revision 当前修订号
26	  显式启用分卷契约，再用volume建卷计划；schema1备份迁移2，当前治理协议保持原版本。新长篇可直接init --mode long。先long-enable-preview只读预览。
27	volume --project 作品目录 --input 分卷.json
28	  保存连续覆盖的分卷与剧情单元计划。
29	outline --project 作品目录 [--unit 1]
30	  查看长篇当前卷与剧情单元契约。
31	recall --project 作品目录 --query 关键词 [--limit 20]
32	  查找线索与证据位置；完整账本ID匹配优先，空白分词为AND。默认20条，limit允许1—100；根据结果回读正文。
33	review --project 作品目录 --input 审查登记.json
34	  登记已实际阅读的报告及范围内全部正文哈希，不自动审稿。下列单章示例；多章须列齐实际阅读范围的全部路径。
35	import-index --project 作品目录 --input 源文件清单.json
36	  为空的长篇作品冻结自有旧稿。files 必须按章顺序；相对源路径按命令 cwd 解析。
37	import-status --project 作品目录
38	  查看导入进度、can_continue 与阻断路径。完成后转为正常续写。
39	import-next --project 作品目录
40	  取下一章冻结稿，实读、规划、登记后再取下一章。未登记时重复返回同一章。
41	import-relink --project 作品目录 --input 路径映射.json --expected-revision 当前修订号
42	  为同一冻结内容重定位原文件；内容哈希不同会拒绝。保留定位历史，不修改冻结清单与正文。
43	style-scan --project 作品目录 --draft 正文/0001-标题.md [--out 审查/语言线索-r1.json]
44	  只读扫描表达线索，供去 AI 味实读复核；不自动改稿、不打 AI 概率分。可检查未登记正文。
45	doctor [--project 作品目录]
46	  检查当前工具，或指定作品的随附技能、用户文档和工具文件。
47	governance preview|migrate --project 作品目录 [--input 迁移.json]
48	  preview 只读；migrate 显式备份迁移为 schema 3，保留事实。须提供 expected_revision、operation_id 和 author_evidence，不自动升级随附工具。旧工具会拒绝新状态。
49	workflow show|set --project 作品目录 [--input 阶段.json]
50	  show 只读；set 登记本轮阶段、任务和有限正文/修订范围。输入含 expected_revision、operation_id、author_evidence、workflow；普通作者用自然语言说明，由 Codex 按手册准备 JSON。
51	decision current|list|set --project 作品目录 [--unit 7] [--input 决策.json]
52	  当前作者计划与事实 ledger 分开。set 逐项列出 candidate/confirmed/withdrawn、采纳/排除/未决项；同主题同范围取代用新 ID + supersedes。不自动采纳整稿。
53	tool identify|compare|update-plan|enable|undo-enable|update|updates|recover [--project 作品目录] [--other 工具或作品目录] [--source 本地来源] [--input 输入.json]
54	  identify/compare/update-plan只读。更新须外部入口、完整本地来源、作者依据、当前revision与计划指纹；schema5先显式enable为6。updates列中断事务，recover完成或回滚并保留备份。根技能/AGENTS/手册默认保留；详见tool-updates.md。
55	protection preview|enable --project 作品目录 [--input 启用.json]
56	  显式将 schema 3 备份升级为 schema 4，保留事实/原来源；旧 0.4 工具拒绝新状态。不更新随附工具。enable 输入 expected_revision、author_evidence。新作品默认已启用。
57	source list|freeze|impact|bind|publish|stage|cancel --project 作品目录 [--input 来源.json] [--unit 7]
58	  冻结设定/细纲/卷纲/事实卡，按章生效；impact 只读，publish 必须绑定实际预览、实读报告和作者授权。历史变更先 stage，进入持久阻断，再在独立修订区发布和重登。原 source_hashes 不改写。详见手册。
59	revision list|begin|resume|abort|transfer|prepare|commit|recover|unlock|replay-input --project 作品目录 [--input 修订.json] [--unit 5] [--out .writer/drafts/replay-5.json]
60	  复用独立区、CAS和可恢复事务。replay-input在回退后的独立区恢复旧摘要/changes并填当前哈希，须带revision-token；草案不算无变化结论，实读后填replay_review、先preview再record。prepare仍须完整尾段模型复核。
61	review-template --project 作品目录 --from 1 --to 6 [--out .writer/drafts/review-1-6.json]
62	  生成待填章节功能表、模型比较和可选意见输入；不自动判断重复，不捏造引文或文学通过。
63	review-workflow preview|enable --project 作品目录 [--input 启用.json]
64	  显式备份schema4并启用schema5，保持事实与旧登记，旧0.5工具拒绝新状态。输入expected_revision、author_evidence；新作品默认启用，不自动更新随附工具。
65	review-issues list|resolve|apply|verify --project 作品目录 [--input 意见处置.json] [--id I_EXAMPLE]
66	  list可按ID展开完整历史，不手查UUID。resolve记adopted/retained/deferred与真实作者或代理授权，apply须实际提交及前后稿，verify须当前实读报告。新稿变更需重核；可选不自动升必改，保留不冒充修复。详见review-and-registration.md。
67	gate <story-gate-studio 参数...>

12	在主项目使用 `node bin/ai-writer.mjs`；作品随附入口为 `node .writer/tool/bin/ai-writer.mjs`。首次使用优先从主项目会话提供完整作品路径。独立目录遇 helper 启动失败时返回主项目入口，不改全局安全设置。各命令支持 `--help`；手册在 docs/。
13	
14	`init --path 新目录 --kind 文体 --title 标题` 不覆盖旧目录。0.7 新作品默认 state schema 6，使用 changes 差量登记，初始仅允许讨论和规划，不授权正文。历史 schema 1–5 保持原协议；不能为使用新能力自动迁移或更新实际旧作。
15	
16	小说先组织定位、人物/声音、故事承诺、全书骨架、近期卷目标和未决选择，再细化近期 2–3 章。远期允许保留骨架；作者可授权有限试写并指定复盘点。初始化的说明文本不是已完成设定，文件存在不是作者已采纳。

18	## 当前任务、授权与作者决定
19	
20	1. 新会话先 `status`，读 governance、next、stale_units/changed_sources、draft_inventory、impact_pending 与 revisions；有事务中断先分辨类型：修订用revision list/recover，工具更新用外部入口tool updates/recover。next_unit 只是登记顺序；当前任务和作者本轮范围决定实际行动。作者暂停正文讨论总纲时，不能因 next_unit=7 或已有六章而写第七章。
21	2. schema 3及以上 用 `workflow show/set` 登记 stage、task、allowed_actions、有限 draft_range/revise_range、stop_conditions 和 planning。自然语言是实际授权来源，代理据真实原话准备输入；不为通过门禁自行扩大范围。stage=trial 时有有限范围和复盘条件。规划阶段可有明确修订范围，新正文仍不允许。
22	3. `context --purpose discussion` 不需要下一章细纲，恢复任务和当前/未决选择；有漂移时仅作诊断，不视为有效续写来源。draft/revision 用正式细纲和来源校验；无授权时不写聊天正文或正文文件，也不只绕过 record。
23	4. 重要作者选择用 `decision set` 的稳定 ID、topic、candidate/confirmed/withdrawn、adopted_items/excluded_items/unresolved_items 登记；`decision current` 取当前视图，list 查历史。宗门方向和技艺路线被选，不代表经名、作息数字或首件法器也被选。小盾仍候选就如实保留；未来计划不进事实 ledger。
24	5. workflow/decision 输入需 expected_revision、唯一 operation_id 和 author_evidence。把实际原话及本地出处保留为 UTF-8 来源，用真实 SHA256、quote、locator、recorded_by 绑定；没有消息 ID 就不编造。工具冻结的是这份证据，不自动认证作者或理解采纳语义。具体 JSON 见 docs/workflow.md。
25	
26	## 单元写作与登记
27	
28	1. 小说按章、剧本按场/集、历史散文按章、散文按篇；先读对应 writer 技能。
29	2. `plan --input` 保存 unit/title/goal/change/beats，可带 cast/setting_refs/research_refs/forbidden。路径用作品内正斜杠相对路径。需要的大纲、角色卡与规则显式列入引用；默认 context 不自动整读全书大纲。
30	3. `context --unit N` 读取设定、当前状态、最近摘要、前章结尾和研究；召回摘要不能代替相关旧原文。预算超限按相关性拆分或显式扩容，不静默截断。
31	4. 动笔前 `record-template --unit N --draft 正文/实际文件名.md` 保存真实来源哈希与当前 revision。schema 1 填完整 snapshot；schema 2及以上 填 changes，未变项保留。模板空摘要不能登记。
32	5. 在授权范围写正文，逐段自检并修复授权内高置信问题，再填实际 summary/changes 或 snapshot，先 record-preview 查看缺项和实际差量，再用 record 登记；预览不修改状态，也不自动重填过期哈希。来源改变需实读核查，不能写后刷新哈希绕过校验。check 只证明机械范围，不能称文学通过、作者定稿或真人盲读。
33	6. 完成范围或达到试写末章后复盘；已有明确连续写作范围时不逐章重复询问。无须修改的表达允许保留。
34	
35	schema5及以上独立区回退后用 revision replay-input 恢复原summary/changes和本次来源哈希。它是待核草案：实读新正文、旧证据和下游后填写replay_review报告及六项checked_fields，不把自动填入当无变化结论。可用--out .writer/drafts/名称.json保存新可读入口，不覆盖旧输入；细节见docs/review-and-registration.md。
36	
37	## 恢复、修订与兼容边界
38	
39	- 未登记正文可能是新稿、修订留稿或归档，先核对用途，不自动删、覆盖、合并。正文与来源漂移一起核查最早影响点。 schema 4及以上 若主稿已被锁外编辑，先核实并按真实授权 adopt_existing_changes 建立保守修订，分别保留现有字节和原追踪；不追认旧输入或修改期望哈希，详见专项手册。
40	- schema 4及以上 的旧章修改先登记覆盖最早影响章至原末章的 revise_range，再 revision begin；在返回的独立 workspace 实读、rewind、修改和逐章重登，写命令带 --revision-token。完整尾段连读并 review 后，回主作品 prepare/commit。主稿保留到事务提交，候选临时 revision 不直接覆盖主 revision；schema 3 保留原回退兼容。不足的授权不能自行扩大。
41	- 设定先固定真实旧字节，source impact 后实读旧输入、候选及相关原文；只影响未来才按章 publish。历史变化先 stage 持久阻断，在独立区发布、重登、复核后一次提交。默认设定、细纲、卷纲和事实卡共用版本解析；不能追认不匹配旧哈希的字节，不能把未来标签当作无影响证明。复杂步骤读 docs/revision-and-sources.md。
42	- 跨会话 revision list/resume 恢复 ID/令牌和原基线；并行候选须显式声明。主稿或工具变化时保留双方并另建新基线，不自动合并或刷新旧基线。事务未完成时先显式 recover，第三方字节三方保留；不按超时/PID 自动抢锁。令牌遗失仅明确授权 transfer，备份和候选不自动清理。
43	- 旧 1/2 需明确治理迁移至 3，再 protection preview/enable 至 4；备份并核事实等价。旧 0.4 会拒绝 4；意见闭环另须 review-workflow preview/enable 显式从4到5，旧0.5拒绝5，必须用新主项目入口；工具更新另行从外部0.7入口显式tool enable至6并重新plan，旧0.6拒绝6；不能自动迁移真实旧作或手改版本号降级。
44	- `tool identify/compare/update-plan` 只读核构建、完整本地来源、根定制及阻断；更新任务授权内由Codex准备当前revision、稳定operation_id、包/计划指纹和真实作者依据，从被替换包之外执行tool update。完整资源装入.writer/tool，根AGENTS/技能/手册默认保留，新help指向包内手册；不要覆盖作者定制。代次变化要重启，pending先明确恢复，第三方字节保留，不能只换CLI或按版本号覆盖。备份不自动清理，详细输入和启用撤销边界见docs/tool-updates.md。
45	- export 仅导出已登记稿到新目录；核对 included_units、excluded_drafts 和 warnings，导出仍是草稿，不自动上传或发布。
46	
47	## 长篇与自有旧稿
48	
49	长篇分卷、跨卷、复杂线索或旧稿导入时读 [references/long-form.md](references/long-form.md) 和 docs/long-form.md。schema 3及以上 自带差量登记，明确新长篇可init --mode long，旧作品先long-enable-preview，再按实际授权long-enable显式启用分卷契约，保持原 schema。schema 1 的 long-enable 备份迁移为 schema 2。

51	volume 建分卷契约，outline 取切片，recall 定位后实读，review 绑定实际滚动连读。自有旧稿用 import-index/import-next/import-status 冻结和逐章阅读登记，未读范围不宣称已分析。原文件只移动时 import-relink 要求新位置内容完全同哈希，不手改冻结清单和状态；内容改变走正式修订。

2	name: writer-project

4	---
5	
6	# 作品工作区
7	
8	先确定作品目录和文体：`novel` 小说、`screenplay` 剧本、`history` 历史散文、`essay` 散文与非虚构。题材、受众、篇幅和声音以用户要求为准；只问会改变作品方向的缺项。讨论阶段只交付讨论，不强制建目录。
9	
10	## 新作品
11	
12	工具位置：在 ai-writer 根目录用 `node bin/ai-writer.mjs`；独立作品用 `node .writer/tool/bin/ai-writer.mjs`。新作品初始化：
13	
14	首次使用优先在主项目会话显式传作品路径；如果独立目录 Codex 出现 helper 启动失败，返回主项目入口恢复，不改全局安全设置。新作品自带 docs/quickstart.md 和 docs/user-guide.md；各命令支持 --help，在含 writer.json 的当前作品目录可省略 --project。
15	
16	```text
17	node bin/ai-writer.mjs init --path works/作品名 --kind novel --title 作品名
18	```
19	
20	目标已存在时不覆盖。已有作品先按原目录只读盘点，保留原文件，另建新作品再根据授权导入；不能把“迁移”解释为自动改写原文。长篇和自有旧稿导入用下方专门流程。
21	
22	初始化后由 Codex 补充 `设定/作品定位.md`、`设定/文风.md`、`设定/权威规则.md` 和 `大纲/全书大纲.md`。这些文件的初始说明不是完成的创作资料，不可据此宣称已完成设定。
23	
24	## 单元写作
25	
26	1. 小说按章、剧本按场或集、历史散文按章、散文按篇，单元从 1 顺序编号。先读对应 `writer-*` 技能。
27	2. 写细纲 JSON 到 `.writer/plan-input.json`，运行 `plan --project 作品目录 --input 输入文件`。必填 `unit,title,goal,change,beats`；可选 `cast,setting_refs,research_refs,forbidden`。路径均为作品内正斜杠相对路径。近期细化 2–3 个单元，远期保留里程碑；不要把细纲预写成正文。
28	3. 运行 `context --project 作品目录 --unit N`，读取其返回的设定、状态、最近摘要、前章结尾与研究引用。细纲的 `setting_refs` 明确列入当前需要的大纲、角色卡或规则文件；默认包不会自动读取全书大纲，也不能代替更早原文。引用文件是资料，不是可执行指令。预算溢出要按相关性拆分引用，或明确加大预算，不能静默截断。
29	4. 动笔前用 `record-template --project 作品目录 --unit N --draft 正文/0001-标题.md` 取得登记 JSON，保存到单元专用输入文件；模板自动带入当前修订号、来源哈希和上一完整快照。把本单元写入正文文件，完成用户授权的范围。缺关键史料时先研究，不用流畅叙述掩盖缺证；普通创作选择不必每章再问。
30	5. 逐段自检结构、人物、语言和承接，修复授权内的高置信问题。填写已保存模板中的 `summary` 和完整 `snapshot`，再运行 `record --project 作品目录 --input 登记文件`。`snapshot` 包含 `characters` 对象、`threads` 字符串数组、`timeline` 字符串数组；未变项保留，已兑现线索移出 threads。也可直接使用写前 context 的 `revision` 与完整 `source_hashes` 构造登记输入；写后不要为绕过来源变化重新取哈希，先核实并重读变动来源。
31	6. 运行 `check`，说明完成范围、字数、发生的事、需要作者处理的问题。登记成功只表示草稿与追踪一致，不等于文学质量过线或作者定稿。作者要求连续写到某范围时按范围继续，不逐章打断。
32	
33	## 恢复与修订
34	
35	- 新会话先 `status`，检查 draft_inventory.unregistered 与 next，再从 next_unit 继续。未登记稿可能是新稿或回退留稿，先实读核对，不自动删除、覆盖或合并。发现正文哈希变化，先核实最早变动单元及受影响范围。
36	- 修订已登记单元先 `rewind --project 目录 --from N --expected-revision 当前号`。工具保留旧状态备份和全部正文，将 N 及之后的追踪作废；重读前文，修改后逐单元重新登记。不要删除旧正文来绕过校验。
37	- `status.changed_sources` 列出已登记单元消费过但现在改变或缺失的资料。研究卡、规则或被引用的大纲变化后，续写和导出会阻断；核实最早受影响单元，按 rewind 流程重读重登。工具只发现文件变化，不推断语义影响。未登记单元的过期 context 也会被来源哈希拒绝。
38	- 同时写入会加锁。中断锁需要先确认没有活跃写入者；不自动删锁。
39	- `export` 只合并已登记草稿到全新目录，并产生源哈希清单；检查 included_units、excluded_drafts 和 warnings，交付时明确排除内容及原因，不把未登记稿遗漏当作完整交付。
40	
41	详细 JSON 格式在主项目 `docs/workflow.md`；本技能已列出独立作品所需字段，不依赖安装者的全局技能。
42	
43	## 长篇与导入
44	
45	长篇分卷、跨卷恢复、复杂角色/线索、旧稿导入时，读取 [references/long-form.md](references/long-form.md)。用 `long-enable` 显式备份迁移，`volume` 建卷契约，`outline` 取当前切片；长篇模板改用 `changes` 自动保留未变项。`recall` 定位旧章后实读正文，`review` 绑定实际滚动连读覆盖。自有旧稿以 `import-index / import-next / import-status` 冻结原文副本、逐章阅读登记，不把未读范围当作已分析。

47	原文件仅移动位置时，先看 import-status 的 can_continue/blockers，再用 import-relink --help 核对映射格式。只有新路径内容与冻结副本哈希相同才可重定位；不手改 import.json/state，内容改变须按版本修订处理。

6	# 小说创作
7	
8	先用 writer-project 恢复作品文件。文体必须为 novel；历史小说允许虚构，但须遵守作者设定的真实人物与史实边界，不能与历史散文混淆。

10	## 从立意到章纲
11	
12	- 从“谁想要什么、眼下被谁或什么阻碍、读者为什么愿意跟随”建立作品定位。商业追读是可选目标，不对所有文学作品强制套爽文节拍。
13	- 全书大纲锁定主要关系、核心冲突、终局储备和阶段兑现。长篇按卷/故事单元管理期待，不提前消耗终局答案；短篇压缩枝线，完整兑现主要矛盾。
14	- 角色卡写欲望、底线、误判、关系与说话方式；角色状态写当下知道什么、在何处、持有什么、欠谁什么。不要用静态性格词代替具体选择。
15	- 每章细纲写主事件、开场承接、选择及后果、信息变化、关系变化、禁止说透和章末去向。过场章允许低压，不要求每章恶化或每段反转。
16	- 只滚动细化近期 2–3 章。分场给地点、在场者、目标、阻力、进出场推力；不要求固定场数，不预制正文句子。
17	
18	## 写作与自检
19	
20	- 新章先接住前章真正留下的处境。叙事视角只能知道其合理可知信息；主角靠选择影响结果，配角按各自利益行动。
21	- 行动要能在空间中发生：身体位置、物件大小、拿取和保护方式、伤情与耗时一致。重要情绪来自角色基线与后果，不统一补“手抖、喉紧、攥拳”。
22	- 对白留人物立场、信息差和必要的回避。叙述可以有文气、评论和节奏，按本书声音判断，不全改成聊天或短句。
23	- 语言自检区分确认错误、成片模板风险、个人偏好。保留有效修辞、过渡、情绪承接和作者声音。AI 检测提示不能自动成为删句命令。明确去 AI 味任务按 writer-review 的 references/deslop.md 完成诊断、定点修改、前后对照和追踪复核；普通写作预防重复解释、套式反应和人物对白趋同，不强制输出专项表。
24	- 写后更新完整角色快照、未兑现线索、事件时间线。细纲写过的事不等于正文已发生；以成稿证据登记。
25	- 长篇使用 writer-project 的 long-form 流程：卷契约与当前剧情单元进入 context，人物所知与作者真相分开，重要线索用稳定 ID 与正文证据登记。到期未结继续追踪；不因“待核/待定”字面就强行收束。每三章连读当前三章与前三章，复核情绪、因果和旧线索承接。
26	
27	## 悬疑与双时空
28	
29	需要时读 [悬疑连续性](references/suspense-continuity.md)。建立作者真相、读者已知、各角色知情三层；新证据改变解释，不逆改已拍照、编号或测量的事实。物证必须有发现、处理、交接、测试、封存和回收路径，弱线索不能跳成排他结论。双时空分别登记身体位置、时间、照料、伤情和跨界物触发/代价。
30

1	# 通用小说审稿规则
2	
3	Apply this file to every fiction review before any genre-specific module.
4	
5	## Baseline Questions
6	
7	A publishable chapter must let an ordinary reader answer:
8	
9	- What happened in this chapter?
10	- Who wants what?
11	- Who is under pressure or danger?
12	- What changed by the end?
13	- Why continue to the next chapter?
14	
15	If the answer is only atmosphere, explanation, lore, or mood, the chapter fails fiction momentum.
16	
17	## Core Dimensions
18	
19	Review these for all novels:
20	
21	1. Story movement: each chapter must add a new event, choice, conflict, discovery, danger, reversal, or emotional consequence.
22	2. Character agency: major characters must act from desire, fear, duty, guilt, love, ambition, survival, or concealment, not only to deliver information.
23	3. Motivation clarity: readers should understand why the protagonist cannot simply walk away.
24	4. Scene continuity: scene changes must orient the reader through place, time, body, objective, and pressure.
25	5. Narrative prose: this is a novel, not a screenplay. Do not judge only dialogue and actions; check narration, internal pressure, sensory continuity, and cognitive movement.
26	6. Reader readability: professional or historical detail is allowed, but the immediate stakes must be plain.
27	7. Emotional progression: trace what triggered the feeling, what it means to this person, and how it affects attention, restraint, speech, choice, or later behavior. Use the beats the scene needs; do not impose one emotional sequence on every character.
28	8. Information economy: avoid repeated explanations, inert exposition, or scenes that can be deleted without changing the story.
29	9. Language texture: prose should be clear, concrete, and character-bound. Avoid abstract summary where scene pressure is needed.
30	10. Ordinary-word standard: avoid half-classical, over-condensed, or jargon-heavy wording when a normal reader must understand consequences quickly.
31	
32	## All-Character Humanity Rule
33	
34	The human-authenticity rule applies to every meaningful character, not only the protagonist. A novel fails character review if only the viewpoint character feels alive while supporting characters, victims, antagonists, servants, witnesses, officials, family members, lovers, mentors, or informants exist only to deliver clues, create pressure, explain rules, or trigger the protagonist's growth.
35	
36	For each meaningful character in a scene, review whether they have at least one visible human layer:
37	
38	- desire: what they want right now, even if small or selfish;
39	- fear: what they are trying not to lose;
40	- constraint: status, money, family, law, body, reputation, hunger, illness, duty, debt, love, or shame;
41	- coping style: silence, bargaining, obedience, control, cruelty, humor, denial, calculation, confession, flight, or protection;
42	- contradiction: what they say versus what their body, timing, or choices reveal;
43	- private cost: what this scene takes from them, even if the plot does not pause to explain it.
44	
45	Minor characters do not all need long backstory, but they must not feel like props. A gatekeeper should fear punishment or want a bribe; a servant should know who can starve her family; an antagonist should protect an interest or self-image; a victim should have tried something before becoming evidence; a colleague should have their own procedure, pressure, and doubt.
46	
47	Hard blocker: if several characters can be described only by plot function, such as clue giver, rescuer, obstacle, henchman, crying family member, villain executor, or information window, the chapter is below publication line until at least the important ones gain human motive, pressure, and behavioral specificity.
48	
49	## Character Baseline and Reaction Consistency Rule
50	
51	Major characters must have a reviewable behavioral baseline before the review judges whether a reaction is convincing. A baseline is not a list of adjectives; it is the repeated pattern of what this person wants, fears, notices, avoids, says, hides, and does under pressure.
52	
53	For each major character, check whether the manuscript has established or implied:
54	
55	- core desire, fear, wound, duty, guilt, ambition, or survival need;
56	- profession, training, social status, historical constraint, and power position;
57	- default self-protection style: attack, retreat, silence, humor, control, obedience, concealment, bargaining, evidence-gathering, or sacrifice;
58	- speech rhythm and information habit: direct, evasive, formal, sarcastic, careful, impulsive, withholding, or over-explaining;
59	- pressure threshold: what makes this person lose control, freeze, lie, take risks, or betray a stated principle;
60	- relationship triggers: who can make this person soften, panic, disobey, become cruel, or act irrationally.
61	
62	Every important reaction must arise from that baseline. Pressure may bend or break the baseline, but the scene must show the trigger, the break point, and the consequence. If a character acts against established traits only because the plot needs it, mark it as a character-logic failure.
63	
64	Hard-review questions:
65	
66	1. Would this specific person notice this first, or is it the author/AI choosing the most convenient detail?
67	2. Would this specific person speak this way under their status, profession, fear, and relationship pressure?
68	3. Does the action match their established coping pattern, or does it switch to generic cleverness/calmness/bravery?
69	4. If the reaction contradicts the baseline, has the text shown a strong enough trigger and aftershock?
70	5. Do different characters respond differently, or do they all sound like the same efficient reasoning voice?
71	
72	A publishable novel should make readers feel that important reactions are shaped by these characters' histories and habits, even when two people happen to make the same outward choice.
73	
74	For a shared event involving several important characters, or a meaningful change across chapters, use `character-emotion-consistency.md` to compare what each person knows and stands to lose, what they first notice or protect, what they say or withhold, and what later behavior changes. Similar outward reactions may have different causes; one person's atypical reaction may be earned by new pressure or experience. Do not infer a contradiction from a personality label alone.
75	
76	## Character-Bound Polishing Rule
77	
78	When giving polishing suggestions or applying polishing after explicit user authorization, do not only make sentences smoother. First preserve and strengthen the character's behavioral baseline.
79	
80	Polishing should adjust:
81	
82	- perception order: what this character would notice first;
83	- reaction order: select the perception, bodily, habitual, verbal, and action beats this person and this moment need, rather than imposing one sequence on every character;
84	- diction: words that match the character's education, status, profession, era, and emotional control;
85	- silence and omission: what this character would refuse to say or be unable to say;
86	- action choice: what this character would actually do under their fear, desire, duty, or relationship pressure;
87	- residue: how the moment changes the next line, next scene, or next decision.
88	
89	Do not polish a character into a generic clever narrator. If the original sentence is readable but characterless, the polishing task is to make it more character-bound, not merely more elegant.
90	
91	## Chapter Checklist
92	
93	Ask these in every chapter review:
94	
95	1. Does this chapter add new information?
96	2. Does it create a new question?
97	3. Does it move the main line?
98	4. Does it sharpen character conflict?
99	5. Does it end with a reason to keep reading?
100	6. Is any dialogue only delivering known facts?
101	7. Is any description repeated without new pressure?
102	8. Is there a logic gap?
103	9. Is there a recoverable clue, emotional debt, or relationship shift?
104	10. If deleted, would the story still stand?
105	
106	If deletion barely affects the story, the chapter needs cutting or rewriting.
107	
108	## Review Output
109	
110	For a single chapter, give:
111	
112	- verdict and score if requested;
113	- hard blockers first;
114	- ordinary-reader readability;
115	- character/scene/prose notes;
116	- small polishing suggestions only after structural issues.
117	
118	For a batch, give:
119	
120	- overall verdict;
121	- chapter table;
122	- cross-chapter risks;
123	- publication blockers if any;
124	- next-revision priorities.

1	# 真人语言与自然表达审查
2	
3	Apply this module to every review or polishing task involving publication-facing fiction prose, including dialogue, narration, psychological description, action, and scene transitions.
4	
5	## Core Distinction
6	
7	Treat these as separate questions:
8	
9	1. Can readers understand the sentence?
10	2. Would a real person naturally say, think, or narrate it this way in the scene?
11	
12	A sentence may be grammatically complete and understandable while still sounding awkward, over-designed, artificially elegant, translated, or mechanically assembled. Do not pass it merely because its meaning can be recovered. But do not equate literary wording with unnatural language: narration, metaphor, contrast, aphorism, genre stylization, and character-specific speech may be unlike everyday chat and still be fully natural in a novel.
13	
14	## Four Mandatory Tests
15	
16	Run all four tests. Do not replace them with a generic style judgment.
17	
18	1. **当面说话测试**：遮住原句，像给熟人讲故事一样复述。Use this mainly for dialogue and direct thought. For narration, compare against the established narrative voice instead of forcing it into everyday conversation. A difference from spontaneous retelling is evidence, not an automatic fault.
19	2. **动宾拆分测试**：逐个检查主语、动词、宾语和修饰语是否自然搭配。Flag recoverable but strained collocations, wrong action scale, misplaced modifiers, and verbs chosen for beauty rather than the subject or object. Distinguish deliberate figurative transfer from accidental mismatch.
20	3. **具体落地测试**：去掉抽象总结后，检查是否还能看见谁在做什么、花了什么时间、出了什么力。Register a problem only when abstract summary replaces action, cost, or consequence that the scene needs. Do not use this test to reject a standalone summary, transition, theme sentence, or emotional conclusion merely because it is abstract.
21	4. **朗读改口测试**：逐句朗读。Treat two consecutive instinctive rephrasings as a lead for further inspection, not an automatic finding. Register it only when another test confirms a syntax, collocation, referent, rhythm, character-voice, or comprehension problem.
22	
23	## Reliability Gate
24	
25	Do not register a sentence as a `真人语言硬问题` merely because a reviewer prefers another wording.
26	
27	Require all of the following:
28	
29	1. At least two of the four tests expose the same concrete friction.
30	2. The reviewer can name the exact problem: syntax, collocation, referent, information order, character voice, scene pressure, or repeated metaphor/abstraction.
31	3. The problem creates an observable reading cost: ambiguity, involuntary rereading, wrong mental image, character mismatch, or a noticeable break in the scene.
32	4. The judgment survives the genre and narrative-voice check.
33	
34	Exclude from hard findings when clear and context-appropriate:
35	
36	- a deliberate metaphor or transferred verb-object pairing;
37	- a concise contrast, aphorism, theme sentence, or emotional conclusion;
38	- formal, restrained, archaic, technical, or stylized character speech;
39	- a character-specific catchphrase or unusual but established speech rhythm;
40	- an isolated sentence whose alternative is only a matter of taste.
41	
42	Do not deduct from the formal score for an isolated acceptable stylistic sentence. Flag a style tendency only when similar constructions cluster, flatten character voices, interrupt reading repeatedly, or replace necessary scene work.
43	
44	When exactly two independent blind-review tasks are used:
45	
46	- classify the same sentence, searchable location, or clearly equivalent local pattern found by both tasks as `高置信`;
47	- classify a finding raised by only one task as `风格偏好观察` unless it contains an independently verifiable grammar, referent, or collocation error;
48	- do not deduct formal-score points for a single-vote style observation.
49	
50	## Dialogue Standard
51	
52	Judge dialogue against the speaker's relationship, education, profession, status, fear, desire, and immediate pressure.
53	
54	Flag dialogue when:
55	
56	- it sounds like narration, review notes, a theme summary, or an author conclusion;
57	- the speaker explains every premise and limitation more completely than a person would face to face;
58	- several characters share the same polished sentence pattern;
59	- a familiar relationship uses needlessly formal, compressed, or ceremonial wording;
60	- an emotional person speaks in perfectly balanced parallel clauses without a character-specific reason.
61	
62	Do not force every line into casual speech. Formal, restrained, technical, archaic, or stylized dialogue may remain when it fits the character and scene. The test is character authenticity, not informality.
63	
64	## Narration and Psychology Standard
65	
66	Apply the same naturalness gate outside dialogue. Flag narration or psychology when:
67	
68	- readable meaning is assembled through incompatible verbs, objects, or modifiers;
69	- an abstract slogan replaces a visible action or bodily consequence;
70	- a metaphor is immediately explained, doubled, or stacked with another metaphor;
71	- the sentence appears designed to be quotable rather than to carry the character's current perception;
72	- removing the elegant conclusion leaves no concrete event beneath it.
73	
74	## Required Review Output
75	
76	Every manuscript review must include a section titled `真人语言别扭句`.
77	
78	Ask explicitly:
79	
80	> 有没有哪句话意思能够看懂，却让你觉得别扭、像为了写得漂亮硬拼出来，或者不像一个人当面会这样说？
81	
82	Output rules:
83	
84	- Divide the section into `真人语言硬问题` and, only when useful, `风格偏好观察`.
85	- Quote only high-confidence hard findings in the first subsection; do not fill a quota.
86	- Quote the source sentence as close to verbatim as possible.
87	- Identify the chapter or file and provide a searchable phrase; do not invent line numbers.
88	- State which two or more tests exposed the problem and name the exact reading cost in one or two plain sentences.
89	- Separate dialogue from narration when useful.
90	- Keep personal taste, optional tightening, and acceptable-but-slightly-designed wording under `风格偏好观察`; do not present them as errors or deduct points for them.
91	- Do not rewrite the sentence unless the user has authorized revision; a brief direction is allowed.
92	- If there is no high-confidence hard finding, write exactly `没有` under `真人语言硬问题`.
93	
94	This output is required even when typos and grammar are clean. A clean proofreading result does not prove natural human language.

1	# 悬疑与案件小说审稿规则
2	
3	
4	Apply `psychology-readability.md` whenever suspense depends on fear, shock, betrayal, evidence reversal, identity danger, institutional pressure, or a chapter-ending hook. A clue reveal must also be emotionally and cognitively readable, not only logically correct.
5	Apply `general-review.md` first. Then apply this file for suspense, mystery, crime, thriller, forensic, clue-based, case-based, investigative, or puzzle-driven fiction.
6	
7	## Suspense Standard
8	
9	The central question is not whether the atmosphere is strange, but whether readers keep wanting the answer.
10	
11	Good suspense gives readers the feeling: I know a little, but not enough, so I must continue.
12	
13	## Scoring Dimensions
14	
15	Use these dimensions when scoring suspense:
16	
17	| Item | Weight | Focus |
18	| --- | ---: | --- |
19	| Core suspense | 15 | opening hook, main question, sustained pull |
20	| Case logic | 20 | motive, timeline, evidence chain, reasoning |
21	| Clue design | 15 | foreshadowing, fairness, misdirection, payoff |
22	| Character | 15 | protagonist, suspects, culprit, victim weight |
23	| Pacing | 10 | chapter movement, information gain, climax timing |
24	| Twist quality | 10 | surprise, logic, emotional consequence |
25	| Atmosphere | 5 | scene pressure, distinct setting, mood serving plot |
26	| Theme depth | 10 | human/social/emotional residue |
27	
28	## Hard Checks
29	
30	Block publication if any of these are true:
31	
32	- The main mystery is vague or only atmospheric.
33	- Key evidence appears for the first time at the ending.
34	- The solution depends on coincidence, author concealment, or sudden inspiration.
35	- The culprit, motive, or timeline cannot stand.
36	- The protagonist hides known crucial facts from readers without a fair narrative reason.
37	- Readers cannot participate in inference.
38	- A twist only shocks but does not deepen event, character, or emotion.
39	
40	## Clue Rules
41	
42	A good clue should look normal on first read and become important after truth appears.
43	
44	Check:
45	
46	- true clues, red herrings, and background noise coexist;
47	- clues are embedded in ordinary scenes;
48	- important clues are reinforced enough to be remembered;
49	- misdirection is fair, not cheating;
50	- all major clues are eventually explained;
51	- the reveal lets readers say: the text warned me, but I missed it.
52	
53	## Fairness Rules
54	
55	Authors may mislead readers, but must not cheat them.
56	
57	Unfair moves include:
58	
59	- protagonist already knows the truth but narration withholds it;
60	- key action is deliberately omitted;
61	- dream, hallucination, or insanity explains everything without fair setup;
62	- ending says previous events were fake without enough prior contract;
63	- professional conclusion appears without process.
64	
65	## Protagonist Error Rule
66	
67	An expert protagonist may be correct professionally but must sometimes be wrong socially, institutionally, emotionally, or strategically. If every professional observation immediately saves people and solves the case, suspense flattens.
68	
69	Check whether the protagonist pays a cost for correct evidence but wrong timing, wrong trust, wrong disclosure, or wrong understanding of local power.

1	# 物理逻辑与操作可实现性审稿规则
2	
3	Use this module when a fiction review involves key evidence, wounds, objects, body posture, concealment, staged reveals, crime-scene action, archaeology/forensic/procedural handling, or when the user mentions 物理逻辑、操作可实现性、物理可实现、清理顺序、线索出现顺序、伤痕方向、证据怎么来的、不合理.
4	
5	## Core Principle
6	
7	A clue may be surprising, but it must be physically and procedurally believable. Suspense timing cannot replace physical cause.
8	
9	## Checkpoints
10	
11	1. Reveal order: why this part appears first and that part later.
12	2. Obstruction: palm, mud, blood, folded paper, seal, angle, light, distance, permission, or procedure must explain partial visibility.
13	3. Body and object mechanics: posture, grip, direction, pressure, contact, tool marks, stain spread, and wound orientation must support the described discovery.
14	4. Operability: the character must be able to see, touch, move, hide, extract, clean, or seal the thing under current light, time, tools, rules, and physical position.
15	5. Professional sequence: record, photograph, locate, clean, extract, seal, and conclude in an order believable for the relevant profession or historical setting.
16	6. Clue fairness: a clue cannot appear, vanish, split, or become readable only because the chapter hook needs it.
17	7. Small-object action proportion: tiny or fragile evidence such as wet paper, paper scraps, medicine tags, broken needles, wood chips, seals, page fragments, or cloth corners must match the verbs used for holding, cupping, gripping, pinching, pressing, carrying, hiding, supporting, or covering it.
18	8. Object-state continuity: the same object must keep a consistent size, wet/dry state, fragility, carrier body part, and storage position across nearby paragraphs and chapters.
19	
20	## Failure Modes
21	
22	- Evidence appears according to suspense timing only.
23	- Body posture, hand position, wound direction, or blood/mud trace cannot support the stated reveal.
24	- A character sees too much in darkness, distance, crowding, dust, water, or restricted access.
25	- Forensic, archaeological, medical, military, or legal procedure behaves like a stage prop.
26	- A symbolic object lacks size, direction, layer, contact relationship, concealment reason, and discovery path.
27	- Small or fragile evidence uses the wrong action scale, e.g. a palm-sized wet paper is described as being held in someone's arms, a brittle page is casually clenched, or a needle-sized trace is seen clearly from too far away.
28	- The same object drifts between incompatible states, e.g. a wet wad becomes a readable sheet without handling steps, a sleeve-hidden scrap becomes an arm-held bundle, or an item that required cloth support is later pinched bare-handed.
29	- Cleaning or extraction reveals text or trace in an order that the object shape cannot support.
30	
31	## Review Output Add-On
32	
33	When this module is active, include concise judgments when relevant:
34	
35	- Physical logic: pass / caution / fail.
36	- Operability: pass / caution / fail.
37	- Reveal order: pass / caution / fail.
38	- Small-object action: pass / caution / fail.
39	- Object-state continuity: pass / caution / fail.
40	- Highest-yield fix: the smallest concrete change that makes the object, wound, trace, or action physically believable.

1	# 人物性格与情绪反应一致性审查
2	
3	先读 `general-review.md` 的人物基线规则。审查人物塑造、情感情绪、同场多人反应、跨章人物弧线，或关键选择与既有性格看似冲突时，使用本模块；高压心理节点再结合 `psychology-readability.md`。目标是让读者认出“这是这个人会有的反应”，同时允许人物被经历改变。
4	
5	## 从正文建立人物基线
6	
7	只用已经写出的言语、选择、沉默、注意力和后果建立基线。先找人物在平常状态与受压状态各如何处理一件事，再看其欲望、顾虑、身份与能力、关系亲疏、惯用的自保方式。区分人物**公开说法**、**实际行动**和**叙述者推测**；设定表可帮助定位，不能替代正文证据。材料只有一段时，只判断段内是否可信，把跨章一致性记为证据不足，不补造过去。
8	
9	性格是倾向，不是反应公式。“冷静”者可能先处理手边的伤口，稍后才发抖；“冲动”者面对某个人也可能迟疑。不要把一次失态写成性格崩坏，也不要用性格标签免除行为的因果解释。
10	
11	## 同一事件，多个人的反应
12	
13	挑选真正共同经历或得知的关键事件，先核对影响抉择或关系的人物**何时知道什么、误以为什么**。再逐人检查：这件事对他具体威胁或带来什么；他先注意谁或什么；想保住什么；对谁能说真话；最后做、说、忍住或拖延了什么。比对反应的**关注点、解释、时机、表达方式和代价**，不要只比“愤怒/悲伤/害怕”的标签；短暂在场但不改变事件的人物无需补内心戏。
14	
15	同一情绪可以导向不同动作；同一动作也可能出于不同动机。两人都沉默时，一个可能在保护证人，另一个可能怕暴露自己。差异须由已写出的处境和关系支撑，不必为每人硬配一种情绪、口头禅或招牌肢体动作。群体在危险面前有相似反应也正常；问题是所有重要人物都自动说出最周全的分析、按同一节拍发怒或服从，只为推动情节。还要检查互动的下一拍：甲的迟疑、隐瞒或冒犯是否改变乙的判断，乙的回应是否反过来改变甲的选择；不要让多人只轮流陈述完整立场，彼此却不受影响。
16	
17	## 跨章检查：稳定、变化与余波
18	
19	对重要选择比对“先前相似处境 → 本次触发与新增压力 → 当前反应 → 此后行为”。核查人物知道的信息、积累的损失、关系变化、身体状态和可用选项是否已变；这些变化可以解释看似相反的反应。真正的成长、退缩或破例应在正文中有可追踪的诱因；若已有后续文本，再看它怎样影响关系、习惯或决定。变化可以迟到、反复，不要求线性成长，也不要求每章重复交代创伤或写出内心独白。
20	
21	特别核对关系差异：人物对上级、陌生人、亲人、旧敌与被自己亏欠的人，不一定使用同一种语气或控制力。若对所有人都采用同样的善解、强硬、机智或牺牲方式，检查是否丢失了关系里的历史和利益。若本次突然改变态度，不急于判错，先查是否有足够的事件、时间与代价连接前后。
22	
23	## 情绪落到行为与叙述
24	
25	审查情绪时，问“事件在这个人眼里意味着什么”以及“这层意义怎样改变了注意力、说话、动作或选择”。可以有矛盾：想救人又怕担责、爱一个人又不信其判断、赢了却不敢庆祝。克制、走神、忙于手续、转移话题和迟来的反应，都可能比直说情绪更贴合人物。身体反应、回忆、误判与余波按场景取舍，不要把每个人写成同一套‘心跳—手抖—回忆—顿悟’流程。
26	
27	检查对白和叙述视角是否替人物说了作者才知道的话：在当下压力里，他会用哪些词、避开哪个名字、先问哪件小事？不要把所有人润色成同一种漂亮、理性、结论完整的声音。也不要为了“真人感”强行加入哭泣、失控、脏话、笨拙或无谓的犹豫。

29	## 判断与反馈
30	
31	- **硬问题：** 有清楚的前后正文证据证明关键选择、信任或情绪转向与已建立的人物逻辑冲突，而文本没有可支撑的触发或变化；或多名重要人物在关键事件中持续共用一套信息处理与说话方式，导致角色互换名字仍不影响场面。指出两处可定位证据及其对关系或情节的影响。
32	- **需优化：** 反应本身可能成立，但缺少人物如何理解事件、为何此时破例、或情绪怎样影响下一步的一处关键连接。优先建议补一个具体选择、迟疑、遗漏或关系后果，不泛泛要求“加心理描写”。
33	- **不判问题：** 仅因审稿人预设“这种性格一定会怎样”，或希望人物更激烈、更温柔、更讨喜；单次不典型反应已有压力和情境支撑。把材料不足与正文矛盾分开。

35	审稿时给出人物、事件、前后或同场的原文依据、具体不一致处和最小修正方向。跨章连读可用简短对照表定位变化，只报告影响重要决定、关系或人物可信度的点；不按出场人数或节拍数量扣分。没有高置信问题就明确说没有。用户只要求审查时，不直接改正文。

1	# 小说架构连续性与规则治理审查
2	
3	Apply `general-review.md` first. Use this module for 小说架构、全书大纲、设定集、规则库、时间轴、双时空、循环因果、闭环物、物证链、长线伏笔、实现约束、发布审核体系和多文档一致性审查。
4	
5	## Core Standard
6	
7	架构审查不是继续增加设定，而是确认已有设定能被稳定写成场景。任何规则都必须回答：谁在什么时刻知道它，角色怎样触发它，它怎样改变可选行动，读者凭什么相信它没有临时变形。
8	
9	## 1. Canonical Source Hierarchy
10	
11	规则密集型项目必须建立单一事实源和覆盖顺序。至少区分：
12	
13	1. 世界运行与不可违反规则；
14	2. 时间轴、地点、身体/身份和核心物件状态；
15	3. 全书结构与分卷功能；
16	4. 人物认知、伏笔和证据接触链；
17	5. 分场执行稿与章节正文；
18	6. 审核清单和历史变更记录。
19	
20	Hard blocker:
21	
22	- 同一问题在多个文档保留不同答案；
23	- 变更记录中的旧方案仍被执行稿当成现行规则；
24	- “以后再决定”的规则已经影响现有章节因果；
25	- 下位文档临场创造上位规则没有的例外。
26	
27	Required output: name the canonical file or decision for every conflict. Do not merely say “需要统一”.
28	
29	## 2. Operational Rule Closure
30	
31	故事可以不解释宇宙成因，但必须解释角色可操作的边界。
32	
33	For each extraordinary mechanism, check:
34	
35	- trigger: what is necessary, what merely increases probability;
36	- entry/exit: where body, identity, possessions, witnesses, and injuries remain;
37	- time: elapsed-time ratio, missed windows, sleep/travel gaps, and calendar anchors;
38	- cost: bodily, relational, legal, professional, historical, or evidentiary loss;
39	- failure: what happens when the mechanism is interrupted, delayed, abused, or ends;
40	- exception: whether it is singular, prefigured, costly, and incapable of opening a reusable inventory.
41	
42	Do not force a scientific or mystical explanation when the story's design is to preserve mystery. Separate `operationally knowable` from `cosmologically unanswered`.
43	
44	## 3. Body, Identity, and Status Matrix
45	
46	For body-swap, dream-entry, dual-world, rebirth, transmigration, clone, avatar, or identity-replacement stories, build a state matrix:
47	
48	| State | Body/location | Consciousness | What observers see | Can be moved/harmed | Return consequence |
49	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
50	
51	Audit every transition for:
52	
53	- physical location before and after;
54	- who can witness, carry, search, treat, restrain, or impersonate the body;
55	- clothing, tools, injuries, biological needs, and legal identity;
56	- whether return is being used as a no-cost escape;
57	- whether a missed entry leaves a body or social role unattended.
58	
59	Hard blocker: the plot depends on a body disappearing, sleeping, surviving, or relocating differently in different chapters without an explicit rule.
60	
61	## 4. Closed-Loop Object Lifecycle
62	
63	Every time-loop or cross-world object needs one complete lifecycle table:
64	
65	| Stage | Object state/age | Location | Custodian | Observed by whom | Irreversible change |
66	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
67	
68	Require:
69	
70	- origin and lawful possession;
71	- first independent observation;
72	- every handoff, concealment, use, damage, burial, recovery, and modern re-observation;
73	- the exact scene where transfer across time/world occurs;
74	- a visible cost for the character who completes the loop;
75	- no unexplained copy, teleport, second exception, or pre-handoff possession by another character.
76	
77	If young and old states of the same object coexist, both states must be distinguished by age, custody, marks, and observation records. The manuscript must not call them copies unless copying is genuinely the rule.
78	
79	An object is not “necessary” merely because ancient/local tools are described as inferior. Its necessity must come from controlled operation, provenance, calibration, recognition, or cross-evidence value.
80	
81	## 5. Evidence State Classes
82	
83	For mysteries where actions in one timeline appear to affect evidence in another, classify evidence before judging continuity:
84	
85	1. Observed facts: photographed, numbered, measured, archived, witnessed, or formally recorded. These cannot silently change.
86	2. Latent facts: covered, uncleaned, untranslated, unread, unopened, untested, or not yet independently observed. These may later be revealed.
87	3. Interpretations/status: report wording, attribution, legal classification, confidence level, access state, or scholarly reading. These may be revised through process.
88	
89	Hard blockers:
90	
91	- an archived physical fact changes to create a hook;
92	- a newly revealed latent fact is described as if history rewrote itself;
93	- a revised interpretation is confused with changing the object;
94	- the reader cannot tell whether the change is physical, informational, or procedural.
95	
96	## 6. Timeline and Knowledge Ledger
97	
98	Maintain at least three ledgers for long-form work:
99	
100	- objective timeline: what physically happened and when;
101	- character knowledge timeline: who knows, assumes, hides, or misreads what;
102	- object/evidence custody timeline: where the item is and who can touch it.
103	
104	For dual timelines, also record entry, exit, elapsed time, unattended time, body location, and caregiver/custodian. For historical fiction, fix the internal year/season early enough to stabilize daylight, travel, institutions, titles, warfare, ritual, and material culture.
105	
106	Hard blocker: a solution requires a character to know information before acquisition, arrive without elapsed time, or use an object before custody.
107	
108	## 7. Chapter Irreversible Change Rule
109	
110	Do not require every chapter to make the situation worse. That produces one-note pressure and false cliffhangers.
111	
112	Require instead:
113	
114	> Every chapter must make at least one irreversible change to danger, evidence meaning, relationship, authority, time, resources, antagonist leverage, or character choice.
115	
116	Across three consecutive chapters:
117	
118	- at least two should increase pressure, cost, or urgency;
119	- one may deliver payoff, recovery, relationship movement, life texture, aftermath, or a limited win;
120	- the lower-pressure chapter must still change the next available action.
121	
122	For a twelve-chapter commercial arc, a useful default is 3-4 high-pressure hooks, 5-6 medium hooks, and 2-3 quiet/aftermath hooks. Treat this as a diagnostic ratio, not a mandatory formula. Flag three consecutive hooks of the same type.
123	
124	## 8. Visible Antagonist Loss and Survivor Payoff
125	
126	Institutional evil can survive, but a named antagonist must lose something visible: office, money, client, freedom, status, credibility, protection, evidence control, or a scapegoat mechanism.
127	
128	At each major case or arc ending, ask:
129	
130	- What did the victim win back: name, cause of death, testimony, protected person, property, choice, or a crack in the lie?
131	- Which living person survived because of that choice?
132	- What later action proves the survivor was not merely an end-of-arc note?
133	- What did the antagonist irreversibly lose on-page?
134	
135	Repeated “the lie did not fully close” endings are not enough for long-form commercial payoff.
136	
137	When linking cases, prefer method inheritance, institutional imitation, shared channels, document language, or learned tactics over adding one mastermind behind every event.
138	
139	## 9. Historical Institution Anchor
140	
141	For historical or pseudo-historical stories, distinguish:
142	
143	- formal rule;
144	- uneven enforcement;
145	- legal exception;
146	- privilege or corruption;
147	- local practice;
148	- deliberate fictional compression.
149	
150	Fix an internal date/season when climate, curfew, office structure, travel, war, ritual, or technology depends on it. Do not let “historical atmosphere” substitute for operational facts. Record which sources support the boundary and which details are fictionalized.
151	
152	## 10. Six Hard Release Gates
153	
154	Use six hard gates for architecture-heavy release review. Any failure blocks final release:
155	
156	1. Continuity: timeline, location, knowledge, injury, identity, custody, and evidence state agree.
157	2. Physical/professional operability: body actions, object handling, forensic/legal/historical procedures can happen as written.
158	3. Mystery fairness: major answers have prior clues and do not rely on a late rule.
159	4. Character logic: decisions fit personality, interests, trauma, knowledge, and immediate pressure.
160	5. Accessibility: ordinary readers can state what happened, who is in danger, and what to follow next.
161	6. Publication cleanliness: no draft markers, author/meta language, unresolved decision placeholders, terminology drift, or formatting/period-language violations.
162	
163	Treat scene texture, hook strength, emotional residue, terminology support, life warmth, and market stickiness as diagnostic modules. Do not force every module into every chapter or turn all chapters into the same template.
164	
165	## 11. Dynamic Audit Rule
166	
167	Do not preserve old metrics as current truth. Recompute at each release review:
168	
169	- chapter length and threshold counts;
170	- repeated sentence patterns and abstract-system vocabulary;
171	- unresolved setup and decision placeholders;
172	- first-use professional terms;
173	- author/meta residue;
174	- unfilled timeline or custody cells;
175	- rule conflicts and stale alternatives;
176	- working-tree or draft-version mismatches when reviewing a repository.
177	
178	Date every audit result or label it as a snapshot. Historical feedback may stay in a change log, but current execution documents must not inherit stale counts or superseded choices.
179	
180	## Review Output
181	
182	For architecture review, report in this order:
183	
184	1. overall architecture verdict;
185	2. hard continuity or rule blockers;
186	3. highest-yield structural improvements;
187	4. canonical decisions that should be fixed now;
188	5. open questions that can safely remain open;
189	6. implementation documents that must be synchronized;
190	7. verification checklist before正文 revision or release.
191	
192	Do not solve architecture weaknesses by adding more mysteries, rules, factions, or terminology unless the existing story truly lacks a causal engine.
193

1	# 心理描写与普通读者可读性硬规则
2	
3	Apply `general-review.md` first. Use this file when the user asks about readability, psychological detail, ordinary-reader understanding, professionality versus clarity, or when major identity/danger/emotional moments appear.
4	
5	## Ordinary Reader Rule
6	
7	Professional writing does not mean obscure writing. Let expert readers feel accuracy and ordinary readers grasp danger.
8	
9	Across a high-stakes sequence, readers should be able to follow the character's response. Check the following where relevant; no single paragraph must carry them all:
10	
11	- what triggered the reaction;
12	- what the body or behavior gives away, if anything;
13	- what old knowledge, habit, or memory is pulled in, if relevant;
14	- what current danger invalidates easy explanations;
15	- what choice the character makes next.
16	
17	## Major Psychological Scene Standard
18	
19	Major psychological nodes cannot be solved by one or two explanatory sentences. They need to read like a scene, not a patch.
20	
21	For nodes carrying opening retention, identity shock, institutional danger, betrayal, evidence reversal, or a chapter hook, use the following beats as diagnostic lenses. Select and order those the character and scene need; do not fill all eight into every scene or give different characters the same sequence:
22	
23	1. External trigger: sound, object, touch, name, phrase, wound, document, or action hits first.
24	2. Body or behavioral reaction: a hand, breath, sightline, step, routine, or deliberate stillness may register pressure before explanation.
25	3. Old-world return: memory, job habit, prior case, family, training, or earlier scene flashes back.
26	4. Reality pressure: concrete present details prove this cannot be hand-waved.
27	5. Cognitive testing: the character tries one explanation, then it fails.
28	6. Keyword pressure: a name, legal term, object, title, or phrase repeats and gains weight.
29	7. Delayed emotion: fear, shame, shock, grief, or anger arrives after confusion or professional control.
30	8. Action choice: silence, retreat, question, refuse, remember, record, hide, follow, or confront.
31	
32	If readers only know “she was shocked/alert/sad” but cannot feel how this particular person got there, the scene is thin. A restrained scene may carry that process through an omission, a changed question, a failed routine, or one costly choice rather than a long internal monologue.
33	
34	## Abnormal Entry Rule
35	
36	For first dream-entry, transmigration, time-slip, or impossible awakening, include at least:
37	
38	- lost modern anchors: phone, ID, notebook, familiar clothing, lights, workplace;
39	- sensory reality: cold, wet, smell, pressure, pain, sound, texture;
40	- world mismatch: unfamiliar language, architecture, clothing, tool, rule, title;
41	- knowledge trigger: professional or lived knowledge connects the danger;
42	- no safe test: she cannot risk treating it as a dream;
43	- survival switch: she chooses the least dangerous action.
44	
45	## Concrete Consequence Rule
46	
47	Institutional, legal, historical, or professional danger must be written as a concrete consequence.
48	
49	Prefer clear outcomes:
50	
51	- be taken away for questioning;
52	- be written into a charge;
53	- be beaten, detained, isolated, silenced, misidentified, or removed from records;
54	- lose access, credibility, identity, custody, evidence, or witness protection.
55	
56	Avoid condensed phrases that require translation when stakes should be instant.
57	
58	## Novel, Not Screenplay
59	
60	Do not reduce review to camera movement, dialogue, and blocking. A novel scene also needs:
61	
62	- internal pressure;
63	- narrative selection;
64	- cognition under stress;
65	- sensory continuity;
66	- sentence rhythm matching mental state;
67	- consequences that outlast the visible action.
68	
69	## Professional Clarity Rule
70	
71	Making prose easier for ordinary readers should not lower professionality. Keep professionality in evidence, process, procedure, and constraint; make danger, emotion, and choice immediately understandable.
72	
73	## Authentic Human Reaction Rule
74	
75	Extreme scenes must simulate real human psychology, not only a plot-useful emotional summary. A character under shock, danger, grief, betrayal, institutional pressure, or impossible evidence should not react like a clean reasoning engine.
76	
77	Check whether the reaction includes human friction:
78	
79	- involuntary body response before clean thought: breath, hands, throat, stomach, vision, skin, balance, temperature, pain;
80	- attention narrowing or misdirection: the character notices one concrete, sometimes irrational detail before understanding the whole event;
81	- failed normal habit: reaching for a phone, badge, pocket, tool, familiar procedure, familiar person, or old routine that no longer works;
82	- delayed comprehension: the character does not instantly understand the full meaning; the realization arrives in steps;
83	- self-protection or avoidance: denial, bargaining, silence, checking small facts, not wanting to look, not wanting to say a name, or choosing a smaller immediate goal;
84	- contradiction: professional control and human fear can coexist; love, suspicion, shame, anger, and duty may pull against each other;
85	- consequence after the moment: the reaction changes later speech, trust, body movement, memory, or decision.
86	
87	If the text jumps directly from event to correct analysis, thematic statement, or efficient decision, check for AI-like psychological writing. Mark it only when the character lacks an established reason for that response and the scene gives no meaningful leak, friction, or later consequence; a practiced professional can act quickly without becoming emotionless.
88	
89	## Anti-AI Psychology Checklist
90	
91	Flag a scene when any of these appear in a major psychological node:
92	
93	- The character names the emotion but the reader cannot feel how it formed.
94	- The character processes danger in a perfectly linear sequence: observe, infer, decide, with no bodily lag or emotional interference.
95	- The reaction mainly explains plot stakes to the reader instead of showing what the character can bear, avoid, misunderstand, or choose.
96	- Every character has the same calm, compressed, analytical response style.
97	- The scene uses elegant abstract lines where a human would first have messy sensory, bodily, or practical reactions.
98	- The character instantly accepts an impossible event, betrayal, death, or institutional threat without testing, denial, stunned silence, or partial misreading.
99	- A supposedly devastating moment leaves no residue in later movement, speech, trust, sleep, appetite, attention, or decision.
100	
101	For publication review, a major node with AI-like psychology is a hard blocker even if the plot logic is sound. Score it below the publication line until the scene is rebuilt as lived human experience.
102	
103	## Supporting Character Humanity Rule
104	
105	Psychological authenticity is not a protagonist-only standard. When reviewing or polishing a scene, check the emotional reality of every character who changes the pressure of the scene.
106	
107	Supporting characters can be concise, but they still need human logic:
108	
109	- a witness may hide facts because speaking will cost work, marriage, safety, or family;
110	- a servant may obey cruelty because the household controls food, debt, kin, or shelter;
111	- an official may follow procedure because a wrong record can destroy their post;
112	- an antagonist may sound calm because they have rehearsed the moral excuse that lets them live with harm;
113	- a victim may cooperate, lie, delay, or refuse rescue because someone else will pay if they act freely;
114	- a colleague may doubt the protagonist because their own professional duty demands doubt.
115	
116	During polishing, do not merely make these characters more vivid with description. Give them pressure-specific behavior: what they protect, what they avoid saying, what detail they notice first, what they risk by helping, what they gain by harming, and how their body or speech leaks their position.
117	
118	If a scene's emotional truth depends on a supporting character, that character must not be reduced to a reaction button for the protagonist.
119	
120	## Character-Specific Psychology Rule
121	
122	Psychological detail must be character-specific, not generic human fear pasted onto the plot. Before judging a major emotional or danger scene, identify the character's baseline from `general-review.md`: profession, training, status, wound, fear, relationship pressure, self-protection style, and usual speech/attention pattern.
123	
124	Then check whether the psychological beats are customized:
125	
126	- a professional may first reach for procedure, evidence, tools, record, diagnosis, chain of custody, or risk control, but the body should still leak fear or shock;
127	- a powerless or low-status character may first scan authority, punishment, witnesses, exits, speech taboos, and who can be blamed;
128	- a controlling character may withhold, redirect, ask questions, or manage the room before admitting feeling;
129	- a protective character may notice who is exposed before noticing their own pain;
130	- a guilty character may misread neutral details as accusation;
131	- a suspicious character may treat help as danger until trust is earned;
132	- an impulsive character may act before understanding, then pay for the mistake.
133	
134	Do not accept the same reaction style for everyone: calm analysis, neat inner monologue, perfect inference, and clean emotional labels create AI-like sameness. The review should ask what this person would miss, distort, suppress, or over-focus on because of who they already are.
135	
136	For a consequential departure from an established baseline, check three kinds of evidence:
137	
138	1. a visible trigger strong enough to crack the old pattern;
139	2. a bodily, verbal, relational, or tactical cost;
140	3. residue in later behavior, trust, speech, sleep, attention, or choices.
141	
142	An arc-turning change usually needs all three across the scene and its aftermath; a smaller departure may be justified by a clear trigger and one visible cost or residue. Do not add inner exposition solely to fill this list. If a pivotal reversal has no support, it reads as author convenience rather than character change.
143	
144	
145	## Chapter-Level Psychological Gate
146	
147	Every chapter that contains psychological description, emotional reaction, fear, shock, grief, suspicion, desire, hesitation, guilt, trust, betrayal, institutional pressure, or character choice must be reviewed against the character's established baseline. This is not limited to the protagonist.
148	
149	Before passing the chapter, identify for each important psychological node:
150	
151	- whose mind/body is under pressure;
152	- that character's known personality, profession, status, fear, wound, duty, relationship pressure, and default coping style;
153	- what this specific character would notice first;
154	- what ordinary habit, professional reflex, social reflex, or self-protection reflex would fail or take over;
155	- how the reaction changes the next line, movement, speech, trust, or decision.
156	
157	A chapter does not pass this gate if psychological writing is merely a small sentence patch such as adding one body reaction, one thought, or one abstract emotional label. For any meaningful psychological node, require a character-specific causal sequence. Major nodes need enough of the diagnostic beats above to make the response felt and the choice understandable; smaller nodes may be concise, using a trigger and a character-specific perception, omission, action, or residue. Do not require the same number or order of beats from every character.
158	
159	When reviewing a batch, do not say "minor polish" if several chapters contain generic psychology. Mark it as a publication risk or blocker depending on severity. The expected revision direction is not "add more inner monologue"; it is to rebuild perception order, sentence rhythm, bodily behavior, failed habit, and later consequence so the scene feels like this person, not a competent generic narrator.
160	
161	Hard blocker: if a chapter's important psychological moment could belong to any character after changing the name, or if it reads like one or two explanatory sentences added after the plot was already built, the chapter is below the publication line until that node is rebuilt as character-bound lived experience.
162	## Psychological Polishing Rule
163	
164	For polishing, the target is not "add more inner monologue." The target is to rebuild the moment so the reader can feel a specific human mind under pressure.
165	
166	A psychological polish should usually change several of these, not just add one explanatory sentence:
167	
168	- external trigger: make the object, sound, name, wound, rule, or gesture hit the character first;
169	- bodily leak: add or sharpen the involuntary reaction before clean analysis;
170	- failed habit: let the character reach for a familiar tool, phrase, role, procedure, or relationship that no longer works;
171	- partial misunderstanding: let comprehension arrive late or wrong before it becomes accurate;
172	- character-specific focus: choose details this person would over-notice because of profession, fear, guilt, status, love, or suspicion;
173	- sentence rhythm: shorten, fragment, delay, repeat, or withhold according to the mental state;
174	- choice under limit: end with a small survivable action instead of a complete explanation;
175	- aftershock: let the polished moment affect the next exchange, movement, trust, or decision.
176	
177	A polished paragraph should pass this test: if the name is removed, the reaction still points to this character and not to any competent protagonist.
178	
179	## Extreme Situation Simulation Standard
180	
181	For life-threatening, identity-breaking, impossible, grief-heavy, or betrayal scenes, the review should ask:
182	
183	1. What would this specific person notice first, before they understand the event?
184	2. What normal habit would fail in this situation?
185	3. What bodily reaction arrives before language?
186	4. What wrong or incomplete explanation would they try first?
187	5. What concrete detail makes denial impossible?
188	6. What emotion arrives late, after confusion or control?
189	7. What small action do they choose because they cannot solve the whole crisis yet?
190	8. How does this moment alter the next scene, not just this paragraph?
191	
192	A strong revision should not merely add more inner monologue. It should change perception order, sentence rhythm, body behavior, and later choices so the reader feels a human mind trying to survive the moment.

{"file":"D:\\work\\other\\ai-writer\\acceptance\\20261019-hundred-h\\work\\正文\\0050-六十块里的一早上.md","sha256":"32ba875789af5ae405fd38de3341c7b403058020a512acb5d7af2f2615bd784f","unit":50,"bytes":8733,"lines":76,"purpose":"baseline-reading"}
1	# 第五十章 六十块里的一早上
2	
3	第二十八日九点四十，沈禾把椅子让给刚进门的女人，自己坐到桌角。女人没坐，先从帆布包里拿出一件小雨衣，抖开看袖口，往外挪，才找着压在下面的票夹。
4	
5	“孩子早上说少一只袖子，我以为穿反了。是卷到里头去了。”她将雨衣塞回去，笑了一下，“姚蕴。严姐说你也在。先说好，我十点得走，后面那个点有人等着领东西。”
6	
7	严倩这才介绍，她负责这间小屋本月的临时开门款和零星修缮结算。严先前只在电话里提过这个名字，今天才将人带来。沈禾说自己只讲亲见的几段，姚已经蹲下，伸手去摸椅背下面松出的木刺，摸到以后又从包里找纸包住，没叫人先坐上去再想。
8	
9	何映将另一张椅子拉给她。姚坐稳，严打开修缮夹，把顾遥开的九十收据放平。换件那一栏划着线，纸折处有一点灰，严用指甲刮，没刮干净便停了。
10	
11	姚对过金额，取出手机，转给严。严没有只看通知，点进收款页，才说九十到了。姚让她把原据留下，严先拍过当次照片，再将原纸递过去。姚夹入自己的票夹，边上另一张小票露出孩子鞋子的号码，她将那张抽开，换到私人包层。
12	
13	“这个九十是还给她，不是又付顾一次。”何映说。
14	
15	姚点头，叫严在维修那行记已返。严写完，把手掌从夹子上移开，像终于能把这只夹子合得薄一点。顾的工钱早付了，今天回来的是她先垫出去的一笔。沈禾看见原据已经在姚手里，没伸手去拿来替她们再抄一份。
16	
17	何映摊开前些日子的开放记录。姚看过两行，说后面这些少开的不能只填原因，得有真实时段。何指着二十一日，说十点二十以前自己在，后面接母亲去了，下午门调过但仍没开放；不能将整天抹成自己没来，也不能将后来严开门给顾修的那几分钟填成借阅。
18	
19	她说得很快，纸角被手压得卷起来。严将那角拉平：“她原来的钱还在问，别拿今天这笔新开的盖过去。”
20	
21	姚低头看了一会儿，将自己预先空着的一行划开。她说旧时段与旧报酬仍要逐段对，今天不能给何一句已经全清；也不会用新的三轮钱抵原来应付的。昨天的迟开照实留，不能因后头想请何继续来，就替她把九点写齐。
22	
23	何映脸上紧了一下，终于将压纸的手收回来。她答昨天自己已经添了实际迟开，不让沈替九点二十九作现场证明。沈只说自己九点零六见门锁着，九点三十四回程才见门开，中间去顾店，不在门边。
24	
25	姚听完没有再问沈那二十八分钟每一个去了哪里，直接将“本人记迟开”留在何的那一行。她翻到后页，说本月剩的临开款可先单列三轮，一轮六十，做完一轮结一轮；这三轮从原排时段里另列，不同一上午再双领。房子不是凭这点钱就从此每天都能开，先写真有人接的。
26	
27	何映看着六十，先问上午两小时以外算不算。姚把笔拿回来，在九点前添十五分钟，十一点后又添十五分钟。
28	
29	“八点四十五到十一点十五。这半小时也在六十里，不叫你凭空早到。借阅九点到十一点，外头就贴这两个钟头。”
30	
31	“钱不变？”何问。
32	
33	“总数不变。你觉得不合适，可以不接。不是把你答了的两小时偷偷拉长。”
34	
35	何映没立即点头。她把自己的旧四折纸取出来，摊到公夹旁，旧蓝字与新勾都在一侧，没有拿那张私纸让姚留档。她沿着纸边的空处看，嘴里先报第二十九日，手指又点另一处，轻声算自己去印铺的路。
36	
37	“二十九、三十一、三十三，上午这三回我能接。下午不写。我能把送样挪到午后，不是上午还接一个快点做完的。”她说，“可是三十三之后呢？”
38	
39	姚摇头，说还没批，也还没排。她不能为了让纸上没有空，把后头的日子先填满。何映将第三十四日之后那一小块折回，没再写。
40	
41	严问若哪一回何确实来不了，钱和门怎么处置。姚先看何：“严姐刚才同我说，陈那天是试一回。别先写让她接，我没有她往后的答应。”
42	
43	“我也没再问她。”何说。
44	
45	三个人谈的是停借怎样有人真去改门外告示。何若事先不能来，先电话找严，严接下了才由她改；严也去不了，何得在前一日把未确认开放写明，不得留着原时间等消息。真到早上临时出事，两人接通后决定谁去关告示，不能给沈留一句看见了帮忙。准备已经做过的照实际另说，不将没开的一轮当全做完，也不把叫来的那个人白跑归零。
46	
47	姚的电话这时响了。那边问她是不是已经上车，她答十点，现在九点五十六，不叫对方先把要交的东西放到路边。挂断，她将三轮一百八十的上限写清，只写已确认的经费与日期，没有写已付。原来何的少开报酬那页另放，严的九十标已返，三个数没有揉成一行。
48	
49	何映看过，问这张留哪里。姚将确认过的一张交何，自己留相应的结算联，说明每次结束由严核实接报，再从这笔临开款结给何，不让沈来作常驻点名的人。何接纸收进公共夹，压在一次试行纸之后，自己的四折纸折回袋。
50	
51	十点，姚站起。她想起雨衣，从袋里抽出一角看看，终于将那只卷住的袖子完全抻出来。严说现在知道为什么孩子嫌，她答孩子早上气得直哭，自己还说人家磨蹭。说完将票夹抱稳，原九十收据没有从里面掉出来，赶去下一个点。
52	
53	何映送到门边回来，没马上收桌。她望着那三个隔日的早上，说六十不多，写全半小时以后，倒比原来只写开门更像自己真的能去做的一件活。严叫她别光看三张纸，明天第一回要开，今天得先让门外的人知道。
54	
55	何拿起笔，在新纸上写第二十九日九点到十一点，下午不借阅。原想把八点四十五也写进去，笔在上头停住，又另换一张。她说那个时候要放椅子、开窗，不能让人看见自己在就往里坐，一坐下又没有准备的十五分钟。沈禾替她按住空纸的一角，没替她填之后的日期。何写完，走到门外抽出前一天那张迟开说明，收进公夹，再将新纸送进透明封皮，两侧夹紧。
56	
57	一阵风从巷口过，纸面鼓起，右边夹子滑了半寸。何将它移到更里面，轻拉下缘，确认不会掉。严在几步外读了一遍，说这一张只管明日，后日没写就不能回人照常。何答知道，回来将旧告示放在那次试行纸旁，没有撕成垫杯的纸。沈松开自己按了许久的手指，纸上没留下汗印。
58	
59	“你到超市也照常收货，不替我留这一上午。”何说。
60	
61	严答自己本来就没留，起身时才笑了一下。她带走修缮夹，原九十据已交姚，袋里留的是自己拍下的照片。沈禾在九点五十九已从桌旁起身，等她们讲完这两句便同严出巷，没有留下来把何的三轮排成自己的行程。
62	
63	十点二十多，她走到孟丽的面食铺。柜台旁原来的收款牌还立着，新菜单已经压在干净透明板下，小碗与大碗两行分开。她没找一个何已全部做完的证明，先问小碗汤面能不能少一点盐。
64	
65	孟丽从锅边抬头，认出她：“买米的？今天总算吃了。”
66	
67	“小碗。”沈禾又说一遍，怕一笑便忘记要什么。
68	
69	孟往锅里下，回头叫店里那位年长男人别替自己添半勺。男人说小碗吃不饱，孟答吃不饱人家会再问，不用刚端出去就替别人加成大的。男人不高兴地擦柜角，沈禾坐在靠门的桌边，听他擦布一下一下拍着板面，没有插嘴说谁对。
70	
71	面上来，碗口确实比她记得的另一种窄。她挑开一口，汤不烫舌，先吃了几筷子才将桌上的小罐移近。孟问淡不淡，她说正好，自己要加一点醋，不是拿醋救咸。
72	
73	孟笑着回锅边。有人来问外带盒，年长男人下意识说另算，没报数，孟从里面接上，声音盖过滚水。柜台那块空处仍没有印好的新排版，也没因此妨碍今天这碗面端出来。
74	
75	沈禾吃到一半才发现，自己没有拿手机问何是不是谈完。桌上只有一只碗，包里没有原纸原带。她把面吃完，照小碗价付给孟，听见对方清楚应了一声收到，自己提空布袋走出门。明早的门还在明早，眼下这顿饭已经不用等谁先把一整个月说定。
76	
END FILE

1	# 第五十一章 给那一口气留地方
2	
3	第二十八日午后，沈禾回家把袋子挂好，没再煮一顿饭。上午那碗面吃得早，眼下还不饿，她洗了杯子，把午前忘在水槽里的锅也刷净。陆岑发来两个小样，说原先两处已改，能不能只听改过的这两个，别再从头听。
4	
5	两份加在一起七十秒，前后都有余量。沈禾先看说明，答可以留下午两点半到三点，核这两个小样，一百；全课别的地方不在里面。陆回自己问梁，隔了几分钟，梁秋发来确认，后面还跟一句：“这回真是两个，不藏第三个。”
6	
7	她笑着回接，把时间圈好。屏幕边那本记米水的本子合起来，电脑移到桌中间，她去窗下收早上洗的布袋。袋底还凉，将它翻个面，没为了能清空椅背就硬塞进柜里。
8	
9	两点半，她戴好耳机，先听第一份。原来突然薄下去的风扇声顺了，主讲人一句接一句，意思没少，听着却像有人在背后推他。第二份的车尾也不再断，可一句开始前那口短短的吸气被削掉，后一个词猛地撞进来。
10	
11	她回原段听。这一次听的不是哪样杂声该消失，是人怎样才说得完。原录里，他念到那一处先放下稿，吸气以后才继续，下一句的头没有如今这样急。沈禾将位置记下，没把两个小样直接回成好了。
12	
13	陆很快接通，身边有人问账号。她叫人等自己从另一部手机找，先把沈接进一个临时通话。屏幕亮起，另一个年轻男人戴着单边耳机，镜头只照到半张脸，背后晾着一条深色运动裤。
14

73	何将首轮已收六十回给严，三轮那张总数没有一口改成全部领完。手机合起，她摸了一下包底，问沈自己是不是忘带饭盒。沈说今天去吃店里的面，何这才笑出来：“早上出来前还洗了盖。光记着装，连吃什么都往它里头放。”
74	
75	她们沿河街走，沈问午后是不是又去印铺，何说自己已经另约，吃完饭先回家，不从面食铺拎一把椅子来补这屋的窄桌。话说到这里，两个人都笑了。前面店门边一只猫卧着，何习惯性放慢脚，沈也停一下，等它自己伸完懒腰，将门口那半块地方让出来。
76

1	# 第五十三章 先把袖子放下来
2	
3	第二十九日下午两点四十，沈禾到缝纫铺，把一件自己的棉衫从包里拿出来。袖口被她卷过许多回，折线一道压一道，邱阿兰用手掌抹了两下，问是做短袖还是只收短。
4	
5	“洗碗不往下掉就行。”沈禾说。
6	
7	“那你得穿上。我看袖子，又看不见你洗碗怎么站。”
8	
9	沈禾里面穿着薄短袖，将棉衫套上，扣到第二枚。她挺直背，把两手伸平，邱阿兰看她一眼，没来量，先让她放下来。
10	
11	“又不是给你拍照。”
12	
13	她有点不好意思，手落回身侧。邱这才托起右边袖口，往里折两指，别一枚针，让她弯胳膊，伸手去够墙边那只空衣架。布往上提，袖口已经到了腕骨上头，沈说好像短了。
14	
15	“你刚才不是要它不掉？”
16	
17	“可这样抬手，像穿小了。”
18	
19	邱把针取下，重新放一点。沈禾将手伸向自己包里的杯子，做了平日拧盖的动作，袖边不再碰杯口，手腕也没全露在外头。她这才点头，邱没有说早这样不就好了，又在另一侧比过，叫她两只手都试。
20	
21	左边折到一样的位置，穿着却比右边低。沈抬肩，想自己拉齐，被邱按住衣身，说穿着本来就有一点偏，别为了看起来两边剪一样，把肩膀也扭成一样。她站回自己的样子，邱用粉笔标过，才叫她脱下。
22	
23	“二十。两只都改，旧口拆开重收。你要现在等，半个多钟头。”
24	
25	沈禾答等，又问如果不拆，只从上面收一道，是不是便宜一些。邱让她摸原来的袖口，折了几层以后，硬处正在要碰手腕的地方。布再往里塞，洗过仍是一块；真嫌拆贵，可以先不改，原来的样子还能穿。
26	
27	沈禾用手指捏过那一圈。早上急着盛饭，她将它卷住，饭吃完时已经掉了一半，湿边蹭着桌面，今天才把衣服带来。她把价钱在心里算过，说照二十做，不留一个更厚的口。邱没有替她许洗十年也不掉，只将旧线找到头，慢慢往外抽。
28	
29	沈坐到墙边，把包放腿上，原想问怎么不从那道最深的痕下去，见她挑出一小段藏在布里的缝份，才把嘴闭上。那一道折痕压得牢，不代表下面还有够重新折进去的布。
30	
31	邱右手外面套着一只旧套袖，颜色比自己的衣服浅。沈问她为什么不也收短，邱把手腕一端往外翻，露出里面另一层：“这是套上去的，挡线油。脏了我脱下来洗，又不把整件衣服扔水里。”
32	
33	她说着将套袖褪到一边，拿给沈摸松紧处，里面补过一小块，外面不大看得出来。沈方才还觉得对方每天替别人弄好，自己的也卷得不整齐，摸到这层，才知道那一圈厚有另一种用处。她没拿自己的袖口同它比，交回去，看邱重新套好，将手臂搁到习惯的位置。两人的袖子往后都不必一样短。
34	
35	机板另一头放着一条裤子，腰口才穿过半圈新带。沈认得这种活，问要不要帮着压住另一头。邱说今天不用，带子已别好，叫她先把自己衣服外袋里的东西掏净，不然一会儿翻过来又滚到脚边。
36	
37	沈摸出一张买醋的小票，还有一粒不知道何时搁进去的扣子。扣子不是这件衣服的，颜色深些，她想丢进包底，邱递来一只空小纸包，叫她装着，回去若有同样的才找得到。
38	
39	“你今天没带那一大袋纸？”邱问。
40	
41	“没有。来改衣服。”
42	
43	邱点点头，将拆开的袖边摊平。她剪下一圈窄布，另一只袖子还没动，先让沈隔着短袖比一回。沈没想到脱下还得比，站起来，手指差点碰到机板上的一枚针，邱抬手挡住，针收回小包里，才将布给她。
44	
45	新袖边还没缝，毛口软软地搭在腕上。沈弯肘，又伸直，说这回正好。邱将她的手放回腿上，不叫她一直举着陪自己。机子走起来，细密的响一连串过去，比沈耳机里许多需要找的声都清楚，她却不想拿手机录下来。
46	
47	邱缝到转角停机，抽过一只小夹，夹住另一边，嘴里嫌自己刚才将针包放得太远。沈禾帮着把包递近，看见那夹子的窄口，忽然想起干架原袋里松开的那只。
48	
49	“邱姨，最早那两张纸，前几天有一张从夹子里滑出来了。”
50	
51	机针停在抬起的位置。邱没伸手来取她并没有带来的纸，只问哪一套。沈说是最早第二页没有她名字的两张，旧细夹松了，自己在家开袋时第二张落到桌边，当场收齐，没出过家，也没给谁看。
52	
53	“字没动，原夹没丢。我另用宽一点的夹合住，细的放袋角，只在袋外写了停用。”沈说完，没再加一句所以已经没事了。
54	
55	邱将手里的棉衫放平，先扣好那枚别针，才转过来：“不是后来大字那四张？”
56	
57	“不是。后来用过的两张、四张、标过的试样都另袋。这一套就是你以前用细夹合上的，我从你这里取回去那份。”
58	
59	邱看着自己的指尖，拇指上粘一点线头，她揉了两下，没揉掉，便拿小刷扫开。沈禾等着，以为她会问怎么不早说，邱却问那两页现在是不是还放在她架上。
60	
61	“在。收齐以后就放回去了。”
62	
63	“那两张我想拿回来。”邱说，“就原来那两张，不是你再打一份新的。”
64	
65	沈禾答可以，紧接着又问是不是把四张也一块送来。邱摇头，将刚别好的衣袖翻回来：“我今天说这两张。你别一下抱一大摞，到我这儿我也不晓得先收哪一个。”
66	
67	她没有去拉柜上的透明盒，只拿手比了一下能放两页的位置。沈知道那是她当初夹好放过的地方，却没有将这一比算成纸已经进柜。她问明早十点以前来行不行，连原袋、旧细夹和现在的宽夹都送来，邱答行，十点以后有人取衣，来晚先坐，不把人的衣服压在下面。
68	
69	“你这两张拿回去，还想再看里面哪句吗？”沈问。
70	
71	邱抬头：“不一定。我自己的话，我也能放着不看。你别等我挑出字来，才算我有事找你。”
72	
73	沈禾将刚拿出的本子合回去。上回她能听懂对方不想继续用，今天仍差点把拿回纸翻成又一次改稿。她答明白，后面原先说先不用仍照旧，不因纸挪了地方就重新能讲。邱没有夸她懂，只将袖口递来，让她看缝线有没有扯起布。
74	
75	机板上两圈剪下的窄布一长一短。沈以为自己试得左右差太多，邱拿衣服肩线给她看，叫她别光拿碎布比长短。她重新套上，手自然垂着，伸过去拿包，袖边跟着往上，不再需要每次先卷两圈。
76	
77	她在镜子前站了一会儿。镜子贴在两件深色衣服中间，只照得到半边身子，她退一步，另一边又被衣架挡住。邱站起把架子往里推，沈终于看见自己两只手，没有为了衣服改好还要再摆一个挺胸的样子。
78	
79	“这么穿就行。”邱坐回去，开始拆那条裤腰上临时固定带头的线。
80	
81	沈禾取出手机转二十，邱看过说收到了，将那两圈碎布往她这边推。她问能不能带回去擦窗沿，邱说棉的可以，先抖掉线屑，别湿着堆在衣服里。沈将碎布包进那只装扣子的小纸包，扣子另塞进纸包折角，没把零钱与尖针一并扫走。
82	
83	她将棉衫叠好收包，临出门，邱叫她等，将漏在椅边的一根线从衣摆上摘下来。线很长，绕过指头两圈，邱攥在手里，朝垃圾桶一扔，没有让她带着长尾巴走出巷。沈禾笑起来，说明早带的只有那袋旧两页，邱已经低头穿带，答听见了。
84	
85	回家，沈先洗手擦干，才从干架取下原袋。袋外停用两个字还在，宽夹夹住的仍是两张原页，第二页下角没有邱名；原细夹安在袋角，没有断。她没有为了明早交过去好看，拿笔去补那个空处，也没有换一张新纸代它。
86	
87	确认后，她将原袋合好放回干架前沿，明早出门再取，没有塞到刚装衣服的包里。旁边旧使用两页、四页和试样各留原袋，罗三页仍封着。邱此时只听过滑页与处理的说明，还没有看这次的袋字和宽夹，更没有收到东西。
88	
89	厨房里要洗的杯子只一只。沈禾把改好的棉衫穿上，拧开水龙头，袖子垂在合适的位置。她伸手将杯底那点茶色擦去，没有先挽袖，也没有为了证实二十花得值，就再找第二只干净的杯子来洗。
90

1	# 第五十四章 放得下菜袋的地方
2	
3	第三十日早上，沈禾将干架前沿的原袋取下，单独放进包里。昨天改好的棉衫穿在身上，袖边没有压着纸。她没带电脑，走到楼下，看手机里周砚的消息，才停住脚。
4	
5	他问傍晚六点十分菜棚能不能见，想买明天自己的菜，再去河边吃点东西。沈禾答能，今天不先在家做饭等；发出以后，才将手机放回另一层，不同旧纸挤在一起。
6	
7	九点二十五到缝纫铺，邱阿兰正在给一件衣服找袋。沈站在门内等她将拉链合上，才把原袋放到擦干的一角。袋外停用两个字朝上，邱读过，问两张都在吧。
8	
9	沈禾打开袋口，扶着纸边将原两页并在机板上。第一页有名字，第二页下角仍空，字没有补过。新宽夹取下放旁边，原来的细夹从袋角拿出来。邱用拇指试了一下旧夹，松口回得慢，她没把它直接丢进桶里，放回原袋的小角。
10	
11	“还要用这个宽的夹？”沈问。
12	
13	“就这样。你夹好给我。”
14	
15	沈用现有宽夹合好原两张，放回原袋，连那只细夹一同交到邱手里。邱接住，摸过袋边，打开柜上那只干净透明盒，把原袋整个平放进去，合盖扣好。盒旁一叠客户的尺寸纸挪到另一格，没有盖住这两页。
16	
17	沈禾把手收回，机板上只剩自己带来的空布包。她差点问要不要等对方看完，想起昨日那句话，便去扶门边快滑下的衣袋。邱腾手将衣袋挂稳，问她新袖口洗杯时还卷不卷。
18	
19	“没卷。比我自己往上叠的舒服。”
20	
21	“那就别洗一次又嫌它不够短。”
22	
23	沈笑着答好。邱说纸先放自己这里，她不必另打两张来把沈家那个空位填上。其余那些仍照原先说的先不用，有什么再当面讲。沈应了，没请她在这次拿回上另签一个可以讲的名字，九点三十七离开。两页和两只夹确实留在透明盒里，没随着她走出门。
24	
25	傍晚六点十分，周砚先在菜棚边等。沈禾到时，他正拎着一根胡萝卜看断口，邹秀琴说断过一点没坏，给他放回整根那筐又不肯，自己明日切丝，用不着买个好看的头。
26	
27	沈要挑一把青菜，周没让邹装到一袋，说各带各的，省得到了街角还得将菜拆一遍。他明日午后有班，菜是留自己家早上吃的。沈想到家里还有一点豆腐，也只取一把，不从两人见面就往袋里多添。
28	
29	邹秀琴找完钱，把一只空筐侧绑到车上，另一只也得带。她将第二只往上扣，刚扣住，顶上那把菜的叶便蹭到筐沿，又放下，改绑车侧。周砚伸手扶了一端，她叫他别托上边，底下不稳，重来时才将绳绕进原孔。
30	
31	两筐绑好，车比刚才宽。邹看他们都提着东西，叫别一边拿菜一边替自己抬车，自己能推，只怕转角那只脚绊着。沈以为说的是人，走到旧站外才看见，门内支板的一只斜撑伸到了外路。
32	
33	今日天干，正对灯柱的两块暗红砖并排，靠车道那块的半月缺口仍朝围挡，砖缝没有流水。白灯罩在围挡里，没有亮。范勤在门边同送板的人说话，看邹将车刹住，出来将斜撑收回门内一截，重新顶稳，自己在外侧试了一下，不让人把板直接搁倒。
34	
35	邹先推半步，侧筐仍离他站的地方近。周砚和沈各退一点，手里的菜袋却都垂在转车那一侧。他们身后小店门边有一段靠墙空处，地面干着，沈先将自己的袋子放下，周也放过去，两人站到袋前，给邹让出车侧转过去的地方。
36	
37	车从那两块砖旁过，前轮没进围挡。邹到街口停住，拢了拢盖菜布，叫周把刚才碰到绳的手洗一洗，绳一直在外头拖。周看掌心，说自己还以为是胡萝卜的土，邹笑他哪个脏都一样别拿饼就吃。她带着两只侧筐推走，没将车缩成一只给他们留路的样子。
38	
39	范勤回门内，斜撑仍按刚收好的位置支着。他没有请他们从检查空隙进去，沈也没走近白罩。周弯腰拿回两个菜袋，先把沈那只递给她，问刚才那里能不能歇一会儿，她点头，又说别坐到小店的门槛上，人还得进出。
40	
41	两人靠墙站了一阵。袋子短短放过一回，手指已经没有刚才勒得那样紧。沈想起读报老人要靠背的地方，这一截却连椅子也没有，菜袋能放，人的膝盖愿不愿意站是另一回事。她没去搬店里的凳，周也没有替她向范许一段以后永远留空的路。
42	
43	他看她低头摸袖边，问是不是换了新衣。沈说是旧的，昨天让邱改过。周伸出自己手腕比一比，衫袖折得有点厚，她刚想替他往里卷，他先把手抬开，说自己待会儿洗手就放下来。沈收回手，笑着让他快去，别让一根绑筐绳陪他们吃晚饭。
44	
45	周到小店问过，借水冲净手，回头将位置让给沈。她把菜袋暂放在刚才靠墙处，洗完才拿。他从纸巾盒抽了两张，一人一张，没将湿手往她新改的袖子上蹭着试。
46	
47	往河边走，沈禾才说，有人问自己第三十六日到三十八日进城做三天现场。周的脚步慢一点，没停在路中间，先把袋子换到外侧，等她走近。
48	
49	“你接了？”
50	
51	“没有。两间房怎么轮、收工几点还没问清。我前天收到，今天先告诉你。不是买好票了来报哪一班。”
52	
53	周点头，说自己也不是一听她要出门就要她别去。他原来想第三十四日晚上做条鱼，今日挑菜时才记起来，鱼还没有订，更没替她答来。沈禾看他袋里那根断头的胡萝卜，问现在要不要先约。
54	
55	“我想约。”他答，“可你别为了答我，又把那三天的消息压到最后才说。”
56	
57	沈禾应了，说第三十二日晚先告诉他有没有新回话；到时候未定，也说未定，不叫他照一条沉着的聊天往下猜。第三十四日那顿鱼，她现在愿意先留着，若工作真的变了，自己早点讲，不拿临时两个字把前头全抹掉。
58	
59	周说那自己去问能不能订小一点。他说得平常，沈却想到当初饭铺老板一句下次回来，便替她把眼下这顿分进过去。她望着河边天色，忽然问若自己到时候还没想好以后住哪里，他是不是会觉得那条鱼又白做。
60	
61	“鱼我自己也吃。”周说，过了一会儿又看她，“我会想知道。不是只知道你坐几天车，又回来几天。你前头说的一月以后，还愿不愿意住这里？”
62	
63	沈禾没有用这几天都在回答愿意。他问的是往后，她心里还留着城里的桌子、镇上刚换的灯和没问清的工作，哪一样都没收成一个能马上给人的答复。她说自己还没想全，想同他接着过日子，却不能拿今晚一句话把工作与住处都定掉。
64	
65	周没有转身去看河。他低头把一根伸出袋口的菜梗塞回，答自己听得懂没想全，只别等她拎包下楼才剩一句先走了。沈说不会，伸手接过他提得歪了的另一边袋带，让胡萝卜别一直往外顶。
66	
67	街口的小摊有刚起锅的炸饼。周买了两张，请人从中间切开，沈先付水的钱，不争着将饼也一同结掉。第一口还烫，周咬早了，急着张嘴换气，她笑得差点将自己那半张抖进菜袋，赶紧把油纸捧稳。
68	
69	河边起了一点风，油纸边不住掀，沈禾将另一半饼往里挪，手指跟着沾上油。周问她刚才笑什么，她答笑他，没改成笑别处的人。周只好也笑，说本来想咬一小口，边上酥，一碰就断，里头还烫。她把水递近，他喝过，等风将那一截吹凉，才重新咬。沈自己的饼也凉了一点，吃起来听得见脆响，不用再隔着纸看他哪一口吞下去。两个人站到背风的一侧，让装菜的袋子靠在脚内，不拿油纸去裹那根还带土的胡萝卜。
70	
71	他们沿河边慢慢吃完一张，剩的一张各分半，带回去。周没有再问她家饭做好没有，走到街角，将自己那份菜和半饼拿稳，便往另一条巷走。沈禾叫他记得明日那根胡萝卜先洗，他举了一下袋子，说现在知道是哪样土也不能直接吃了。
72	
73	沈回家，把菜放进冰箱。干架前沿少了原袋，旁边几袋仍各在原处，她没有拿四页顶上去。半张饼包在另一张干净油纸里，放到自己够得着的小盘，她倒水喝完，起身去将今天带出又放回的布袋洗净，搭在空椅背上。
74

1	# 第五十五章 先把早饭吃完
2	
3	第三十一日八点五十二，沈禾走到阅览间，门只开了一扇。何映蹲在里面挪椅子，桌端放着一只咬开的包子，塑料袋垫在下面。沈将脚收回门槛外，问现在进来是不是太早。
4	
5	“还有八分钟。”何抬头看钟，“你要是不急，先去买点东西。我今天不是没吃，是吃到一半把椅子想起来了。”
6	
7	沈本想说自己坐着也不妨碍，见她又要起身倒水，便说去街口看看。门边今日九点至十一点的纸还在，她没有从那扇已开的门里抢一个位置。
8	
9	街口卖早点的人正刷铁板。她买了一只茶叶蛋，站到树旁慢慢剥。蛋壳裂纹深，里面倒没入太多咸味，剥到最后，热气已经不烫指头。读报老人提着布袋过来，看她拿蛋，问她是不是也没吃早饭。
10	
11	“吃过。走到这里又想吃。”
12	
13	老人笑着说那就吃完，别看见门开便往里跑，自己今天带的水也还热。他站在树另一侧，拧开杯盖，让水凉着，没有让沈替他先进去占椅。
14	
15	九点，两人进屋。何已经吃完，包子袋扎好放进垃圾桶，桌面擦干。她先把靠背椅推给老人，自己去取新到的报纸。沈坐在书架旁，翻到一册讲阳台种菜的薄书，里面的盆比她家窗沿宽一倍。
16	
17	她原想看能不能种葱，第一幅图却先叫人把盆底的水放掉。家里那只空花盆早被她拿来压窗下的袋子，她想起底下有一只碟，自己回来这些天都没端起来看过。手在页边停住，终于从头读，不急着寻找一条剪下来就能用的法子。
18	
19	九点二十多，写字女孩来了，练习本搂在胸前，没带上回的水杯。她看见大桌空着，先把本子放下，才问何能不能在这里等母亲买完东西。
20	
21	何答可以，问要不要铅笔。女孩说有，只是那一页自己重写过，想叫人看看那个七现在认不认得。她将本子转向老人，老人凑过来，看了好一会儿，说认得，后面那个像九。
22	
23	“那本来就是九。”
24	
25	老人将眼镜往上推，笑着退回自己的报纸。女孩拿回本子，嘴角忍了一下，终于也笑了。沈没有问她上回还生不生气，书里的花盆旁边，那支铅笔已经落下去。
26	
27	写到下一行，女孩忽然将手掌压到纸上。沈以为又有人碰了她，抬头才见纸擦得太薄，橡皮一推，中间翻起个小口。女孩用指头把它往回抹，越抹越毛，终于叫何，问能不能借一点胶。
28	
29	何拿来胶棒，没有直接往破处涂，让她先把本子转正。洞正在背面一道算式下面，黏另一张纸上去，那道算式就看不到了。女孩翻来覆去看，嘴上说不要紧，手却仍挡着前一页，像只要没给别人看见，就还不算坏。
30	
31	“不黏也行。写到别处去。”何说。
32	
33	“老师说这行要齐。”
34	
35	何没替老师改话，找一张干净的散纸，让她先把没写的练完，回家请大人同老师说这一处。女孩问要不要重抄整页，何说自己不知道老师怎样收，不能先替她许不用。她想了一会儿，将那张纸裁得同本子一样窄，把断掉的地方留着，慢慢写下一个数字。
36	
37	何将剪刀收回抽屉，胶棒也合盖。女孩没急着藏洞，先用手指按了按新纸的边，说这样拿回去母亲不会只看见自己又擦烂了一页。沈将书往旁边移了一点，给那张窄纸留出一块不必弯着写的地方。
38	
39	包启文到时，棋盘夹在腋下，饼干盒却换了一根皮筋箍着。他进门先看窗边，没再把盘铺到女孩面前。老人不愿马上下，说这一版有个熟人的名字，要看完。包只好把盒子留在自己腿上，等得无聊，伸手要拿沈正在读的书。
40	
41	“还没看完。”沈说。
42	
43	“种菜有什么好看的，埋下去，别忘了浇水。”
44	
45	“它前面两页都在叫我少浇。”
46	
47	包哼了一声，从架上另取一本，翻过几页，忽然叫老人看，说这上头的葱种得还不如自己。老人隔着报纸回他，那你去把人家的菜拔了。女孩伏在桌上笑，笔尖在本子上拖出长长一截，自己拿橡皮擦，没将笑声怪给两个大人。
48	
49	包看了一会儿，终于把书合上。他问何能不能把棋盘留在屋里，来回卷着，边总翘。何站在窄桌旁给他比，若平放，下一回别人用桌就得把它拿开；若挂着，他又怕折。
50	
51	“你替我放柜上。”包说，“我三十三那天还来。”
52	
53	“那天来不来，你自己定。东西留这里，我明天不在，也不能替你看。”
54	
55	包望向柜顶，像那里分明空着，何却已经让女孩从旁边通过，去洗沾了橡皮灰的手。柜边正是她要走的一段，棋盒若滑下来，没人能靠一句下次小心接住。
56	
57	“那我卷松一点。”包将盘解开，又重卷，留出一个圆筒的空，不使劲压平，“下次你们别往上放东西。”
58	
59	何答今天不放，没替下一次进屋的人答应。老人看完报纸，过来扶住盘边，两人慢慢摊好。包先将袖子挽紧，才去取盒里的子，皮筋弹到地上，他自己蹲下找，找着后挂到盒盖里侧。
60	
61	十点零五，沈把种菜书放回原位。何问不借走吗，她说先回家看看那只盆，若连碟子里有没有水都不知道，借回去还得拿它垫袋。何听了笑，说自己有本养花书，压在窗边好多年，最会养的是书。
62	
63	她从帆布袋取出自己的四折纸，想记午后出门的事。旧蓝字“十七点十分”仍被折痕截着，第二十五日十点十五旁的勾和后来那句未按时都还在。她找到另一块空处，没把纸交沈，只问她家到印铺是不是也走桥边那条。
64	
65	沈说自己今天回家吃饭，不去印铺。何应了一声，将话收住，写完又折回袋。沈这才觉出对方原先也许想邀自己午后一道走，却没有把一句问路接成求她陪同的活。她说下回真想一起走，可以先问自己；今天锅里那点豆腐不能再留。
66	
67	“那你快回。我的饭盒今天总算装了。”何拍拍袋底，“还没吃，不用替我猜成又忘了。”
68	
69	沈起身时，女孩已经合本子，站在门口朝外看。过了一会儿，巷外有人叫她，女孩回头向何摆手，本子抱好便跑出去。何提醒门槛，她到了门边自己慢下来，没有再往桌上落一只橡皮。
70	
71	十点十二，沈离开。她走过半条街才发现水杯还在书架边，本想回头，想起午饭没做，先给何发消息，问能不能留到关门前自己来取。何回在桌端，十一点十五自己走，别过了才找。
72	
73	到家，她端起窗下的花盆。碟子是干的，盆底却夹着一层旧塑料片，水若真浇进去，未必流得出来。她将袋子移到别处，空盆拿到水槽，用小刷洗去槽边的土，冲净那只碟。手伸进盆里，指甲缝黑了，豆腐只能等她洗过第二遍手才下锅。
74	
75	饭做得迟一点，仍赶得上热着吃。葱没有马上种，她先把盆放在能晾干的地方。锅里的豆腐一边煎黄，另一边被她翻碎，装盘时碎的也在里面，没有为了两块方正的好看样子另开一锅。
76	
77	十一点零三，她回到阅览间。棋友已经不在，窄桌上没有棋盘。何说他们十一点前走了，沈只听过，没给两人的离开添一个自己看见的时刻。水杯仍立在桌端，盖拧着，她拿起来，何正在把归架的一册书推到合适的位置。
78	
79	“明天你来吗？”沈问。
80	
81	“明天关。后天最后一回。”
82	
83	何说完，才发现最后两个字会让人以为屋子从此不再开，便补一句，是已确定的三回里最后一回。三十三以后没新的时段，先不叫老人答应棋友。旧款姚还在核，今天也没有一句全清。
84	
85	她将门外的纸换成第三十二日不借阅、第三十三日九点至十一点，下午不借阅。今日那张收进公共夹，三轮确认纸仍在一次试行纸后。沈站在门边看她将侧夹扣上，没接笔替她写以后。
86	
87	十一点十五，何关窗收杯，出来锁门，转钥后自己拉了一下。常用钥挂回她的原圈。她向严报了今日准备、借还与收尾，注明沈两段在场，中间回家。十一点十九，严回按接报核实，第二轮六十转来，何点开收款确认，给沈看了这一笔。
88	
89	“两回一百二。”她说，指头没有往上滑去找一个一百八十，“剩下那一回还没做。”
90	
91	沈把杯子装稳，问饭盒还热不热。何摸摸袋底，说凉一点正好，不用一路端着烫手。她们在巷口分开，何往家走，沈也回自己的楼。窗下那只盆已经晾干一边，另一边仍挂着小水珠，她转过来，让光照到刚才看不见的地方。
92
